We are located in Waimea (Big Island), Hawaii. July 14, 2026 Academy Swim Club is a fun, rewarding, and well-recognized competitive swim training program for boys and girls ages seven and up. The vision of our coaching staff is to provide a program that builds confidence in our young athletes, equipping them with the tools to succeed in all aspects of life, while adhering to USA Swimming SafeSport standards. We believe in providing a safe and supportive environment that protects children as they develop. Our mission is to provide swimmers with the training they need to improve their swimming skills and race performance, as well as opportunities to develop their character, grit, perseverance, kindness, and ability to thrive in adversity, while fostering a supportive team environment. text: North County Aquatics Home Southern California Swimming Sign in Instagram Home About NCA Coaches Time Standards Team Records Swim Programs Duck Pond Lesson Group Little Dragons/White Dragons Bronze Dragons Silver Dragons Gold/Platinum Dragons Summer League Calendar Meet Information Support Welcome to North County Aquatics Swim Club Swim Club in Paso Robles, CA North County Aquatics is a premier youth swim program and swim club in Paso Robles, serving families throughout the Central Coast and North County San Luis Obispo. Our mission is simple: to provide a high-quality swim experience that helps every swimmer—from beginning swim lessons to advanced swim practice—build confidence, strength, and lifelong swim safety skills. As a non-profit swim organization, North County Aquatics offers a welcoming, positive environment where kids of all ages and ability levels can thrive. Whether your child is just learning to swim, preparing for competitive swimming, or training at an advanced level, our experienced coaches focus on proper technique, personal growth, and a love for the water. NCA practices at the Paso Robles Sports Club, featuring an 8-lane, 25-yard pool with a dedicated shallow lesson area—perfect for both youth swim lessons and structured swim club practices. Practices run Monday–Thursday from 4:00–6:00 pm for all groups, with Saturday morning sessions for advanced swimmers. Seasonal group swim lessons are also available to help new swimmers safely transition onto the team. SCROLL THE PATH TO EXCELLENCE STARTS HERE. Santa Clarita's Premier Swim Club. Top 100 Club in the U.S. From 2023-2024 Start Your Path Here! ABOUT PASEO At Paseo Aquatics, we're more than just a swim team—we're a supportive community where dreams and water converge. Whether you're diving into the pool for the first time, looking to stay in shape during the off-season, or going for Olympic glory, our inclusive team environment inspires and empowers swimmers at every level. USA Swimming Youth Competitive Year-Round Program; join at any time. High-quality, professional coaching. Various programs for ages 5-18. Safe, fun, family-friendly environment. PHILOSOPHY The Path to Excellence is a 360-degree holistic development program that embodies far more than just swimming. Paseo provides customized coaching, performance opportunities, and monthly Athlete Self-Reflection sessions to engage swimmers and optimize progress. We prioritize “whole child” development: mental resilience, emotional intelligence, intrinsic motivation + overall well-being. Our goal is to nurture champions who embody integrity, perseverance, and teamwork, both in and out of the water. OUR PARTNERS Code: PaseoHBF25 TRAINING & FACILITIES Santa Clarita Aquatic Center The Santa Clarita Aquatic Center features a 50-meter competition pool and a 25-meter dive pool for Paseo's competitive teams. The pools are heated year-round and offer four locker rooms. Castaic The Castaic Aquatic Center offers a competition-sized pool and a recreation pool for Paseo's competitive teams. The pools are heated year-round and feature two locker rooms. Santa Clarita Aquatic Center The Santa Clarita Aquatic Center features a 50-meter competition pool and a 25-meter dive pool for Paseo's competitive teams. The pools are heated year-round and offer four locker rooms. 1/2 Find Your Fit! Join the 'Path to Excellence' at any point along your swim journey. Learn to Swim Discovery Team ​ Beginner swimmers start with an introduction to training and a technique-focused approach to improve all four competitive strokes and racing skills. text: Patriot Swim Club Home About us Our Coaches Careers Explore Lessons & Programs Patriot Swim Club Welcome to Patriot Swim Club - where growth, skill development and a genuine love for the water come together in a supportive and inspiring environment. Our mission is to help athletes reach their full potential both in and out of the water by promoting excellence, integrity, teamwork, and sportsmanship. We pride ourselves on creating a positive environment where athletes learn, grow, and gain lifelong skills through the sport of swimming. Please take a lap around our website to learn more about programs for both youth and adults - from learn to swim programs to competitive racing teams. Explore Lessons & Programs Summer Camps - Learn More ❤️ Loved by 500+ swimmers. Speedo swimwear delivers streamlined performance, innovative materials, and iconic style—built for speed, confidence, and comfort in every stroke. Here is the link where our athletes are recommended to purchase their equipment—all of which is Speedo-brand , which is where our partnership comes from. By selecting Speedo as our official partner, it means we will be promoting the Speedo brand for all competitive and pre-competitive in-water activities . Place order here About the Club Our Mission Patriot Aquatics is committed to creating a highly competitive athletic environment in an atmosphere instilled with high ethical values. Through world-class coaching, Patriot Aquatics strives to build self-esteem, character, teamwork, and a strong work ethic, and we encourage our student-athletes to apply these values to all aspects of their lives. Why Patriot? Through world-class coaching, Patriot Aquatics strives to build self-esteem, character, teamwork, and a strong work ethic, and we encourage our student-athletes to apply these values to all aspects of their lives. Our Facilities Patriot Aquatics offers state-of-the-art facilities for athletes to train and compete at their best. Our regulation-size indoor pool provides optimal training conditions, while our fully-equipped weight room allows players to build strength and power. Our dedicated team room provides a space for athletes to socialize, strategize, and relax before and after practice. We maintain a high standard of cleanliness and safety in all our facilities, ensuring a comfortable and conducive training environment for all our members. JOIN THE SWIM CLUB Learn More SWIM TEAM Joining a swim team is a fantastic opportunity to get involved in swimming at a young age and can be a transformational experience for your kids, offering a multitude of benefits. Swimming clubs offer a tremendous team spirit, not just among the kids in the pool but also between the parents who all share a common interest of seeing their children and the club do well. SWIMMING SCHOOL Swimming is an important life skill that children and adults should learn as early as possible. There are many benefits in learning how to swim and it is an extremely important safety skill. Swimming is a unique activity that has the longevity of being a great form of exercise for toddlers, seniors and everyone in between. Swim lessons are important because they help teach your child proper swimming techniques, but also because it encourages them to be independent in the water. ADULT SWIMMING PROGRAMS "MASTER SWIM" Are you in search of a swimming experience that transcends boundaries and caters to all skill levels? Look no further than “Master Swim.” Whether you’re just starting your aquatic journey or you’re a seasoned swimmer, our program offers a comprehensive and inclusive solution to meet your needs. ADULT LEARN-TO-SWIM CURRICULUM Welcome to our Adult Learn-to-Swim Program, designed to cater to learners at three distinct levels: Level A (Entry Level), Level B (Mid-Advanced), and Level C (getting ready for the Master Program). Our program ensures a tailored and progressive learning experience for adults eager to become proficient swimmers or even join our Master Program. Meet Our Coaches Coaches are certified by USA swim and Red Cross - Safety Training for Swim Coaches SWIM COACH SEBASTIAN CORDOBA VALENCIA Head swim coach Coach Sebastian Cordoba brings a legacy of passion, skill, and dedication as the head coach of Patriot Swim Club. Born in Colombia, Sebastian’s swimming journey began in the warm waters of his hometown, where his mother instilled in him a love for swimming. By age 14, he was already teaching swim lessons, uncovering his natural talent for coaching and a gift for inspiring others. Today, with over 20 years of experience, he embodies a blend of dedication, technical expertise, and infectious enthusiasm that ignites Patriot Swim Club’s competitive spirit. Sebastian’s early athletic career was marked by exceptional talent across multiple sports. At just 10, he earned a place on his state’s team in European handball, volleyball, and water polo, eventually focusing his passion on aquatics. His commitment took him to the Colombian National Team in water polo, where he represented his country internationally in Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico. This level of competition fueled his understanding of high-performance athletics, knowledge he now shares with Patriot Swim Club swimmers. After moving to the U.S. at 19, Sebastian continued his education and swim training at American River College in California, where he competed in the 2007 and 2008 State Championships. His journey continued at Vanguard University, where he earned a dual sports scholarship in water polo and swimming. As captain of Vanguard’s water polo team, he led his squad to Nationals, and in swimming, he excelled as part of a 200 freestyle relay team that placed in the top 10 nationally. Graduating with a degree in Business Administration and Marketing, Sebastian’s academic and athletic balance became the cornerstone of his coaching philosophy. Beyond his role as a seasoned coach, Sebastian is also a father with a vision. He founded and developed Patriot Swim Club to create a path for his daughter, Camila, and all young swimmers like her to compete at the highest levels of swimming. With over 20 years of experience, Sebastian’s journey—from representing the Colombian National Team in water polo to leading Vanguard University’s swim and water polo teams—has shaped a unique coaching philosophy. He’s committed to bringing every swimmer the same level of opportunity, growth, and guidance he strives to give his own daughter. With over a decade in coaching, Sebastian is a trusted leader within the Irvine swim community. Known for his meticulous approach to technique, his focus on building personal connections, and his unwavering support for each swimmer’s journey, Coach Sebastian emphasizes an environment where athletes feel encouraged to achieve greatness both in and out of the pool. His philosophy extends beyond the lanes, encouraging swimmers to excel academically and prioritize their holistic growth. Joining Patriot Swim Club means becoming part of a team driven by excellence, inclusivity, and passion. Coach Sebastian has designed a program that supports swimmers at every level—whether you’re diving in for the first time or training for elite competition. His leadership is built on values of teamwork, resilience, and joy in the sport, helping every Patriot swimmer thrive. So, if you’re ready to push your limits, join Coach Sebastian and the Patriot Swim Club family. Under his guidance, you’ll grow as an athlete, achieve your goals, and make memories that last a lifetime. The pool is ready—are you? Jump in and start your journey with Coach Sebastian today! ACTING PRESIDENT DUJE GRUBISIC Coach Duje: The Foundation of Patriot Swim Club Coach Duje isn’t just the president of Patriot Swim Club—he’s the cornerstone of its success. His unwavering vision has shaped a program designed for swimmers to thrive, compete, and reach their full potential. With the strategic addition of Coach Sebastian, he has cultivated an environment that fosters excellence both in and out of the pool, setting a high standard for the club’s legacy. Coach Duje’s swimming journey began at just five years old with the esteemed Jadran Split Swim Club in Croatia. By the age of 12, he had already made waves as a top-three breaststroker and butterfly swimmer in his region and ranked among Croatia’s top 20 in his age group. His passion for the sport extended to open-water swimming, where he dominated marathon events, securing victories in the 10-and-under, 11-and-under, and 12-and-under categories. After a successful and fulfilling swimming career, Coach Duje transitioned to water polo at the age of 12, where his love for aquatic sports continued to flourish. Today, he remains a dedicated water polo coach, blending his expertise in both swimming and water polo to inspire and mentor athletes. As the active president of Patriot Swim Club, Coach Duje's leadership is the driving force behind the program’s growth, creating a legacy of competitive spirit and community. For more on Coach Duje’s water polo achievements, be sure to check out his bio under the Water Polo section. Read more about Duje SWIM COACH PAULA FERNANDEZ Elite Experience, Passion for Coaching Originally from Barcelona, Spain, Coach Paula Galceran began her swimming career at Club Natació Sabadell, one of Spain’s most prestigious aquatic clubs. Her early start in the sport, coupled with attending a specialized high school for aquatic athletes, allowed Paula to train and compete at an elite level from a young age. This high-performance environment shaped her into a disciplined and skilled swimmer, experiences that she now passes on to her athletes at Patriot Swim Club. After moving to the United States to pursue her collegiate career, Paula competed in both swimming and water polo, further expanding her knowledge of aquatic sports. Paula’s competitive background, along with her training as a coach, including completing an ASCA course on freestyle, allows her to bring a high level of technical expertise to her swimmers. Paula’s passion for swimming is infectious, and she believes that swimming not only builds physical strength but also instills confidence, discipline, and a strong sense of community. As a coach, she is dedicated to creating a positive and motivating environment, where swimmers are encouraged to push their limits and develop both their technical skills and love for the sport. With her international perspective and deep competitive experience, Paula is a valuable asset to the Patriot Swim Club team, ready to guide the next generation of swimmers to success. SWIM COACH IAN PISOR Coach Ian brings a lifetime of swimming expertise and a love for teaching to the Patriot Swim Club. Beginning his swim journey at just five years old, he developed his competitive spirit through high school swimming, culminating in CIF championship competitions in San Diego. Today, as an active member of the UCI club swim team, Ian continues to excel in his signature strokes: backstroke and butterfly. In addition to his swimming accomplishments, Ian is a dedicated student of chemistry and biology at UCI. This academic background enhances his understanding of biomechanics and performance, bringing a unique edge to his coaching. Known for his attention to detail, Ian is passionate about guiding young swimmers in mastering body balance, underwater efficiency, precise turns, and powerful dives—technical skills that serve as the foundation for success in competitive swimming. With Ian, swimmers not only build their technique but also gain confidence and a deep appreciation for the sport. His goal is to create an environment where swimmers push beyond their limits, learn the value of discipline, and, most importantly, enjoy every moment in the water. text: Renegade Aquatics Home Facebook Twitter Instagram Coaches Site Map Sign in Official Site of RENEGADE AQUATICS, Escondido's Competitive Swim Team San Diego-Imperial Swimming Home News Swim Meets Events Pool Locations Baker B&G Club Pool Adams Park Pool Swim Groups Team Records Links Safe Sport-x slide show Renegade Aquatics is a coach-owned, year-round swim team, based in Escondido CA. With athletes from Valley Center, San Marcos, Vista, and other communities, our program draws swimmers from throughout North County. The number 1 priority of our coaching staff is the athlete. We focus on the FUNdamentals when working with your children. We will teach your swimmers the basic requirements of our sport in a safe, friendly, and educational environment. The coaching staff will work on swimming technique and skill development, helping the swimmers get faster as they compete against other USA Swim teams from San Diego county (and beyond). Renegade Aquatics conducted their first practices in September, 2013 and has quickly grown to over 250 swimmers. And we have room for more! If you are interested in joining our program, please contact Coach John McGlynn ( [email protected] ). You can also visit us at renegadeaquatics.com and also on Shutterfly at renegadeaquatics.shutterfly.com Mission Statement The mission of Renegade Aquatics is to provide a safe environment and strong foundation for growth, for all levels of swimmers, so that our participants develop and appreciation for the sport of swimming, respect for their teammates and competitors, and a goal to reach their fullest potential. Team Vision The vision for Renegade Aquatics' swim program is to create an atmosphere which encourages our athletes to set goals, train for those goals in a safe environment, and to meet or exceed those goals by the end of each season. Our entry level novice swimmers will be introduced to our sport in a fun, supportive, and educational setting - where they will learn the basic fundamentals of swimming technique, be encouraged to participate in meets, and learn about the tremendous history of USA Swimming. Our more advanced swimmers will focus on their training so that they can represent our program at the highest level possible: LSC championships, Zones and All Star teams, Sectionals, and hopefully somday National Championships and Olympic Trials. All of our swimmers will strive to promote sportsmanship and show respect to their teammates, coaches, parents, competitors, officials, and spectators. The Renegade Aquatics coaching staff will make every effort to create an environment where the parents trust us to work with your children and allow us to maximize the potential in each individual swimmer. The coaches will seek educational opportunities which will allow them to keep up to date with the latest training techniques and make themselves available to parents to answer and questions about our program. The parents in Renegade Aquatics will strive to be supportive of our swimmers and coaches, providing encouragement and volunteering whenever possible to help improve our program. Parents are often asked to work at swim meets: as timers, officials, or a variety of other positions. And there are also opportunities to work with our Rengade Parent Boosters. If we think of our program as a triangle (with athletes, coaches, and parents comprising the three sides) and each side supports and recognizes the importance of the other two sides, we will build the foundation for a very successful swim program - one that will continue to grow and offer tremendous opportunities for the children of San Diego's North County! title: South Orange County Aquatics Home
text: South Orange County Aquatics Home Facebook Twitter Instagram Sign in Southern California Swimming Home About Us South Orange County Aquatics South Orange County Aquatics (SOCA) was founded as a year-round competitive swim team with a focus on swimmer development, quality coaching, family, and creating a positive environment both in and out of the water. Over the years, SOCA grew into a strong swimming community and helped athletes of all levels develop their skills, confidence, and love for the sport. As SOCA enters its next chapter, our focus is expanding beyond the traditional year-round competitive team. Today, SOCA provides developmental, seasonal, and community-based swimming opportunities throughout South Orange County, including swim lessons, private lessons, seasonal programs, clinics, summer swimming, Masters, and other opportunities designed to keep swimmers learning, progressing, and connected to the sport. For swimmers ready to pursue year-round competitive swimming , SOCA also provides a pathway to Evolution Racing Club , where Coach Kevin Clements has joined the coaching staff and continues to work with swimmers as they take the next step in their competitive swimming journey. We are the longest running USA Swimming in our area. We are unique in that we offer both sports under one team and strive to build on that strength. In our well rounded program athletes have competed at the Regional and National level (Olympic Trials), as well as the age group Junior Olympics level. BSW was founded to provide training, instruction and encouragement for increased proficiency in competitive aquatic sports; to further the interest, education and participation in such sports in the community; to encourage and develop good sportsmanship, individual integrity and team play in aquatic sports; to promote and advance aquatic sports and to combat juvenile delinquency through the promotion of aquatic sports. Our goal is to create an environment where young athletes will gain the exposure, technique, skills, and confidence in swimming and water polo, enabling them to be competitive at the high school and collegiate level. We aim to contribute to the building of well-rounded adults. We believe in building team camaraderie and developing friendships through sports. We hold an annual team potluck in the summer, go ice skating, have movie nights, tie-dye shirts and enjoy many other fun activities together. Text Area Simple formatted text Mission Statement The SeaWolves provide a safe, supportive and positive environment for all members to achieve their highest potential, both in and out of the water. We encourage community, family and individual participation at all levels. Brentwood SeaWolves fully supports all measures adopted by the US Center for Safe Sport and USA Swimming, with the sole purpose of protecting all athletes from any form of abuse or mistreatment. Welcome to the Butte Tarpon Swim Team or BTST for short. BTST is one of the oldest competitive swim teams in Montana and is a member of Montana Swimming and USA Swimming. It was originally known as the Butte America Swim Club. The team has been represented by numerous state, sectional, and zone champions; state record holders; national competitors; and an outstanding group of swimmers, coaches, parents, and volunteers. BTST is also the home swim team of Paralympic gold medalist, IPC world champion, and IPC world record holder Erin Popovich who competed in the Sydney, Athens, and Beijing Paralymic Games. The team has had several persons serve as elected members of the Montana Swimming Board of Directors and has had several members also serve on USA Swimming national committees. Susan Huckeby was selected as an official for the 2020-2021 US Olympic Trials - Swimming. The mission of the Butte Tarpon Swim Team is to promote competitive swimming and develop each swimmer's abilities to their fullest potential. BTST supports the core values of USA Swimming: Build the Base, Promote the Sport, and Achieve Competitive Success. At BTST, we believe swimming is fun, friends and fitness; competition, improving skills, reaching goals, and personal challenges; and sportsmanship, building self-esteem, and quality coaching. Our team values teamwork, sportsmanship, healthy competition, mutual respect, communication, open discussion of ideas, achieving short and long term goals, team pride, cooperation, excellence, problem solving for the betterment of the team, and operating the team with a solid financial plan. Our parents are a fun, supportive and cooperative group who value good communication and open discussion of ideas, serve as volunteers and officials at meets, fundraisers, and team activities; and assist the team to achieve excellence. Parents are always encouraged to be involved with the team. Our coaches provide opportunities for our athletes to achieve competitive success, excel in and out of the pool, become leaders, achieve short and long term goals, and provide a cohesive coaching staff to meet the needs of all our athletes. Our coaches continue to improve themselves through ongoing training provided by USA Swimming, the American Swim Coaches Association, and other organizations. The Butte Tarpons are a non-profit tax exempt 501 (c) 3 organization originally organized as the Butte America Swim Club in March 1978. Donations are gladly accepted and are tax deductible. Progression of the Athlete: STAC SwimFit By Thomas Conner • August 9, 2023 How to Evaluate a Swim Race at a Non-Focus Meet “That Swim Stunk” By Thomas Conner • August 9, 2023 How to Evaluate a Swim Race at a Non-Focus Meet Resetting Goals After a Successful or Maybe Not So-Successful Season By Thomas Conner • August 9, 2023 Coming off the short course season and starting Long Course is a perfect time to take a deep breath and ask yourself as a swimmer “OK. How am I doing? What have I done? Where am I going?” Swimming can be just as mentally taxing as physically, so a healthy conversation and reflection on your achievements or disappointments the previous season is a great way to clear your head. We can’t do anything about the previous season’s results. What can we do to exceed our accomplishments from the short course season or avoid a repeat of the feelings of disappointment? The first thing to remember about a disappointing season is that everything in life can be a stepping stone or a cliff. That extends beyond the confines of a swimming pool. Failure or disappointment is not unique to swimming, and there will never be a single moment in your life where failure marks the end if you do not let it. Taking tangible lessons from the season, August to March, can help shape these tough lessons into a positive outlook moving forward. An untimely injury or illness, a break in focus and consistency in practice due to outside stress, or performance anxiety can all lead to or compound this. Did we work on our swimming weaknesses, be it technique or training , as much as our strengths? Could we be more open to making changes in our eating or sleeping habits to help our practices? Could we improve our time management so that school stress doesn’t affect us in the pool? Any number of changes can help lead a swimmer to a successful season. Identifying what may have held us back before is a great first step. Sometimes it can be more difficult to reset the goals after a great season that ended on a high note. It could be a new time standard achieved, a State or Southern Premier title, or any long sought goal in your favorite event. The question now is how can we sustain this momentum and replicate the success? Again, making note of what improvements we made to our training or habits may help identify not only what made this season so great, but show what other areas may need to be improved to supplement our improvements. Thinking about new stepping stone goals to go along with our new long term goal can help sustain that feeling that we are still succeeding, and that our next goal isn’t so much a mountain as it is a molehill. text: Home - ECSC Skip to content ECSC Home FAQ Joining ECSC Sponsoring ECSC Alumni College Swimming Alumni Records Safe Sport Contact Welcome Members! ECSC Account Pending Alumni Calendar Coaches College Swimming (Alumni) College Swimming- Alumni Contact Contact- ECSC News ECSC Sponsors FAQ Home Join ECSC Site Registration Member Login Password Reset Profile Practice Schedule Records Records- Resources Safe Sport Sponsors Welcome Eugene City Swim Club ECSC Register for the 2026-27 season now! ECSC provides opportunities for each athlete to achieve their full and ultimate potential through proper training in a positive, safe, and healthy environment. Welcome to ECSC Eugene City Swim Club (ECSC), is a year-round competitive swimming team offering instruction, training, and competition to swimmers of all abilities. ECSC is a non-profit organization financed and supported by its members and corporate sponsors, and receives no public funding from the City of Eugene to pay for its use of public facilities. Since the club’s inception in 1968, the program has helped to develop the abilities of many of the area’s finest swimmers. Club members have included numerous nationally ranked age group and senior swimmers, as well as college and university standouts. The team competes in local, regional, national, and international competitions sanctioned by United States Swimming (USA), our national governing body for amateur swimming. We are very proud of our rich tradition and history. Why a Phoenix? ECSC disappeared for almost a decade when we merged with the Eugene YMCA, and has recently been re-established in the state of Oregon. This come-back would not have been possible without an amazing amount of support from the local business community, coaching community, past and present swim families, and a fantastic group of swimmers and families who didn't want to quit. Striving for Excellence Eugene City Swim Club strives to make a positive difference in the lives of its team members by promoting good sportsmanship, mechanically sound techniques, a healthy and nutritional lifestyle, balance, commitment, responsibility, love for the sport of swimming, and self respect. We are committed to creating an environment where every swimmer can realize his or her own potential. We believe that the healthiest motivation for a child is the motivation that comes from within. Our goal is to draw out each child’s natural energy, hope and courage, thereby fueling the pursuit of their dreams. “Not everyone can be an Olympian, but we can be Olympic in our pursuit of excellence.” Sportsmanship -Understands the importance of the ‘team’ -Congratulates teammates regularly during practice and competition -Demonstrates proper meet behavior (i.e. not throwing cap, goggles, etc) -Respectful to Meet Officials -Swimmers know names of competitors Social and Personal Skills – Understands and takes responsibility for attendance and performance, habits in practice and how these relate to meet performance – Respectful of pools, locker rooms, team equipment and other swimmers property – Swimmer is not influenced by the negative behavior/actions of teammates Team Commitment – Actions show dedication to the team and promote team values – Competes in the highest level of competition qualified – Takes leadership positions as positive role modeling for younger swimmers Expectations in Training Technique – Can complete a legal 200 of each stroke – Can complete a legal 400 IM with transition turns – Knows advance stroke drills – Understands relationship between distance per stroke, stroke rate, and swimming speed – Able to maintain stroke rate and times in training sets Expectations in Racing – Can race in every distance, every stroke available over duration of season – Knows his/her best times and best events – Consistent use of race strategy – Maximizes outside factors for better performance Expectations of Training Knowledge – Knows how to descend and build – Sets season goals – Knows what decreasing resistance means – Develop leadership skills – Understands the difference between aerobic and anaerobic training Nutrition – Brings a water bottle to every practice for proper hydration – Understands the importance of proper pre-meet meals – Demonstrates eating a balanced diet and basic fuels used during swimming training Time Management – Swimming is becoming highest priority – Informs coach of practice absences and reasons – Demonstrates proper rest habits Stress Management – Prioritizes schoolwork, social activities, and other commitments including swimming. Meet the Coaches! Nothing has greater influence on the quality of team swimming than the excellence of the coaching staff. Scott Kerr Scott Kerr is a native Oregonian who has a long history of successful swimming and coaching. He graduated from South Salem High School, where he held numerous school swimming records, and was inducted into the school Hall of Fame in 2011. After graduating from high school, Scott competed for the Florida State Seminoles, and in 1987 he received his B.S. in Hospitality Management from Florida International University. Scott’s coaching history includes 4 years at the Pinecrest School in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, 24 years coaching Sheldon high school swimming, 15 years as Head Coach with the Eugene City Swim Club (ECSC), and 9 years as Head Coach with Team Eugene Aquatics after ECSC and the Eugene Y swim team merged in 2009. Scott is an ASCA Level 5 coach and has been part of the USA National Team coaching staff. Throughout his long career, Scott has qualified athletes for the Olympic Festival, World Championships (short course and long course), Goodwill Games, and Olympic Trials. He has coached 13 Senior National Qualifiers and over 60 Junior National Qualifiers. Scott has been married for 28 years to his wife, Toni. They have 2 sons, a dog, a cat, a bearded dragon, countless fish, a rabbit, and 3 chickens. Scott and Toni are NOT currently looking to rescue more pets. Steve Johnson Steve Johnson has coached swimming at six different clubs starting in 1965. Coach Johnson was away from coaching for many years while working as a scientist and university professor. He founded Emerald Aquatics in 1995 and was their senior coach from 2016 until recently joining our staff. In addition to coaching he has a long record of competitive swimming himself, both as a Division One college athlete and as a master swimmer. He has held seven United States Masters National Records. He graduated from the University of Oregon in 1970 and also holds a Ph.D. In sociology. In coaching he tries to help each athlete see that limits are self imposed and that they can do more than they thought possible. Coach Johnson has competed in more than 300 open water swims and won several USMS national championships. He also had top three finishes 4 times at the masters world championship. Stephanie Marler Stephanie Marler grew up on the Southern Oregon Coast and began swimming with the South Coast Aquatic Team at age 10. Stephanie was a varsity swimmer for Marshfield High School in Coos Bay for all 4 years. Stephanie is a graduate of the University of Oregon with degrees in Political Science and Sociology. In 2010, Stephanie began as assistant coach for Marshfield High School, where she coached for over 10 years. During that time, Stephanie also coached for Gold Coast Swim Team and Southwestern Oregon Community College. Stephanie took a short break from coaching when she moved with her family to the Willamette Valley. Stephanie started as the Age Group coach for Eugene City Swim Club in September 2023. Outside of coaching, Stephanie enjoys spending time with her husband and daughter, lap swimming, attending U of O sporting events, and going to concerts. Megan Hummel Megan grew up in Eugene and started swimming on Coach Scott’s team when she was six years old. She swam for South Eugene High School where she was the girls’ team captain during her senior year. Megan also played water polo during high school. She has been a coach with Eugene City Swim Club since 2023 and coaches the Supersquad group. Megan has worked for City of Eugene Recreation since 2016 and currently coordinates the swim lesson program at Echo Hollow Pool. Outside of swimming, Megan enjoys reading, Dungeons & Dragons, watching football, and hanging out with friends and her cats, Meatball and Pablo. Sierra Tena Sierra Tena was born and raised in Eugene, Oregon and found her passion for swimming very early in life. She swam for River Road Swim Club starting at age 6 and continued through her senior year of high school. In addition to club swimming, she was on North Eugene High School’s swim and water polo teams all 4 years of school. Throughout her time with RRSC, she found her passion for teaching as she began teaching swim lessons part time. During her senior year of high school, she began coaching with ECSC as a volunteer coach until she graduated in 2022. From then, she continued as an assistant coach with ECSC as she continues her education at the University of Oregon with a Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Studies. Currently, she works with the City of Eugene as a Swim Lessons Coordinator, Lifeguard, and everything in between outside of ECSC practices! Off the pool deck, you can find her out in the backcountry doing various activities such as hiking, kayaking, paddle boarding, and backpacking. She loves to travel and visit places in our great outdoors as much as she can. She is always looking to learn new outdoors skills and try something new! Volunteering ECSC currently operates on the generosity of our parents and swimmers stepping up when needed. Our ONLY volunteering request at this time is to help out when our team is assigned lanes (for timing) at swim meets. Fundraising We currently have NO MINIMUM requirement for fundraising, and we fully acknowledge that this wouldn’t be possible without the generosity of our families, our community, and local businesses who support ECSC’s core values and goals for our swimmers. We greatly appreciate the ongoing efforts that help keep ECSC alive and well. Still Undecided? Try us out! We assume that by now, you have seen and read enough to be seriously interested. If you’ve never been on a swim team before, and you want to test the waters at Eugene City Swim Club, we invite you to swim with us for two weeks… FOR FREE! Just Visiting? If you swim for another team and you’re visiting from out of town, and you need to stay in the water… we welcome you as well! Please call or email Scott to let him know in advance. He may want to check in with your coach if you’re in a crucial training stage of the season. We look forward to meeting you! ECSC, a member of United States Swimming, encourages athletes to succeed as competitors in the pool as well as citizens of their communities. While natural athletic talent is not bestowed in equal amounts, excellence is an attainable goal for everyone willing to work for it. Sponsors ECSC is a 501(c)(3) organization and would not exist without the generosity of our sponsors. Your contributions keep us going, keeps our fees low for everyone, and allow more families to participate in this amazing, life-long sport. Click to read more! Contact Us If you have any questions about becoming a sponsor, donating to our cause, visiting from another team, or joining our team, please contact Scott Kerr. He'll either answer your questions or point you to someone who can. Click for contact information. USA Safe Sport Reporting Information To deal with a Safe Sport concern , contact USA Swimming at (719) 866-4578 Contact the U.S. Center for Safe Sport to make a report. Call (720) 524-5640 or use the online reporting form or find more information at http://www.uscenterforsafesprot.org/ Please contact our Safe Sport Club Coordinator, Jules DeGiulio, at 541-510-2937 Donate to ECSC We thank you in advance for your support! Your donations are greatly appreciated and will be used to help us grow as an organization while we focus on the present and future successes of our swimmers. Coming soon! Please Help Amount raised: $1,180.00 Goal amount: $20,000.00 Mission Statement: "One TEAM, One Heart " ❤ ❤ ❤ Swimming is more than a recreational activity or competitive sport; it is a pathway to developing essential life skills. By embracing the philosophy that swimming prepares individuals for life, we empower swimmers to become well-rounded, confident, and resilient individuals who can adapt, collaborate, and excel in all facets of life. Through a safe and supportive environment, lessons learned in the water will equip the swimmers with the tools to make a positive impact on their own lives and the lives of others. Heartland Swim Association provides the most comprehensive swimming program in the San Diego area, with programs which cover all aspects of competitive swimming. Our full-time staff of professional coaches train swimmers that range in ability from the beginning competitive swimmer to National qualifiers. For over forty-five years, as a non-profit organization, Heartland has provided enriching programs for area youth. No prior competitive experience is necessary. Each swimmer is placed in a group matching their age and skill level. All levels receive professional training and instruction. All pools are heated year-round to a comfortable 80 degrees. To find out more about our teams check out the General Information tab. Established in 1969, Laramie Swim Club (LSC) is comprised of both the Swim America lessons and USA Swimming competitive club. The Swim America program is designed to teach youth swimming skills until they reach proficiency. Once proficiency is reached, a swimmer is eligible to participate in a swim club to further develop their skills. LSC encourages youth of all levels and abilities to participate in Swim America and club swimming. The club's goal is to provide a safe and supportive environment where youth can improve their swimming skills and abilities. Developing team spirit, individual pride, and sportsmanship are also essential components of our program. Our club is committed to serving all levels of swimmers whether it be to gain confidence in the water, improve swimming skills, or compete competitively. LSC is a non-profit organization run by an elected Board of Directors. LSC operates year-round and is an affiliate of USA and Wyoming Swimming. USA Swimming is the National Governing Body for the sport of swimming in the United States. It is a service organization that promotes the culture of swimming by creating opportunities for swimmers and coaches of all backgrounds to participate and advance in the sport through teams, events, and education. All LSC coaches, competitive swimmers, officials, and board of directors are USA Swimming members and follow the USA Swimming codes of conduct and Safe Sport practices. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact a LSC board member or coach. All members are welcome at monthly board meetings and encouraged to be involved in team activities and fundraisers. text: Mavericks Swimming Association Home Sign in Home Mavericks Swim Club Swim Groups Club Calendar Coaches Registration Adult Lap Swim Swim Lessons Mavericks Swim Store Pool Location Contact Us Donate Welcome to Mavericks Swimming! Mavericks Swimming Association is a 501(c)(3) Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation located in Half Moon Bay, California since 1998. Our mission is to grow a thriving swimming program for all levels and ages in our community. Each year Mavericks Swim Club trains over 150 young athletes from elementary school to high school. Our certified and credentialed coaches provide year-round, age-specific practice groups to challenge and develop each swimmer to the best of their ability. Participation in local swim meets is encouraged but not required. Practices are available every weekday and Saturday. Swimmers can attend as many practices as they want. We offer scholarships for those that qualify. Each week Mavericks Adult Lap Swim offers twenty hours of lifeguard supervised pool time to over two hundred residents of Half Moon Bay for training, physical fitness, and rehabilitation. For over twenty-five years, Mavericks Swimming Association has maintained and funded the Cabrillo Unified School District pool, making it possible for Half Moon Bay High School to offer swim and water polo teams for hundreds of students, as well as swim and water safety classes to all students as part of the school's physical education program. Throughout the year, Mavericks Swimming Association sponsors the Half Moon Bay Boys and Girls Club, the Half Moon Bay Junior Lifeguards, the San Mateo County “Learn to Swim” program, and numerous other community organizations. title: The Olympic Club – The Olympic Club
text: The Olympic Club – The Olympic Club Skip to content Menu Golf Athletics Private Events Public Events Guest Info History Guest Info Foundation Contact Member Login Members Welcome To The Olympic Club Founded in 1860, The Olympic Club’s rich heritage of sporting achievements, its iconic clubhouses and world-renowned golf courses have made it the premier athletic club in the country. Scroll Unwind. Explore. Indulge. Endless Experiences The home of world renowned and iconic golf courses, historic clubhouses housing state-of-the-art fitness facilities and dining options, at The Olympic Club, membership is an active experience. Golf Members can play any of our three iconic golf courses, which have hosted numerous U.S. Opens, U.S. Amateurs and will host the 2028 PGA Championship and the 2033 Ryder Cup. Learn More Athletics Our two clubhouses feature health and fitness facilities, three pools, handball, squash and tennis courts and two basketball courts. We host public athletic events each year. Learn More Hotel Rooms Members and their guests have access to 18 elegantly appointed hotel rooms at our City Clubhouse. Guests enjoy full use of the City Clubhouse athletic, massage and dining facilities. Learn More World Class amenities Our Clubhouses In the Heart of San Francisco City Clubhouse The Club’s first permanent clubhouse on Post Street opened in 1893, but was destroyed in the great 1906 earthquake and fire. The clubhouse was rebuilt and reopened in 1912, and now features a five-lane pool in the iconic Natatorium, a fitness center, hotel facilities, handball and squash courts, circuit training facilities, two basketball courts and full sized swimming pool. Learn More AT the Pacific Ocean Lakeside The Olympic Club’s Lakeside property, located just steps away from the Pacific Ocean, is the home of our three iconic and world-class golf courses, the Lake, Ocean and Cliffs Courses. Lakeside also features eight tennis courts and a clubhouse that houses spectacular dining and banquet facilities, meeting rooms, locker rooms, an exercise center, massage services and a swimming pool. Learn More Host Your Events Have Fun and Celebrate! Whether it’s a bridal shower, wedding, retirement party, or other celebratory event, The Olympic Club’s expert event staff take the stress out of hosting your affair. From small birthday parties for 20 to a corporate event for 800, the Club has the skill, staff and service experience to handle all occasions. Memorable moments City Clubhouse Celebrations Whether it’s a speaker luncheon, cocktail hour, business seminar, or even a wedding, the experienced City Clubhouse team is ready to guide you through all the details of your event. We offer eight different spaces and tantalizing menu options to create a memorable experience for you and your guests. Learn More host in style Making Memories at Lakeside Our Lakeside Clubhouse offers beautiful panoramic views as you enjoy weddings, receptions and private events. Lakeside also offers a marvelous array of catering services, and our team of experts will assist you with planning for your very special event. Learn More become a member Join The Olympic Club Membership at The Olympic Club is open to anybody eight years of age and older that goes through the official membership process. There are several membership categories, each of which may have different privileges and dues obligations. Become a Member The Olympic Club is one of the oldest and most well-respected amateur athletic clubs in the world, where for more than 160 years, our more than 11,000 members have fostered amateur athletics in a spirit of close harmony, camaraderie and teamwork.  查看详情 塑胶制品安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 注塑行业模具管理非常重要，对模具的使用、修模、改模、模具保养等需要做全面管理，色粉色母的配比管理及领用，水口料的回收、粉碎和重复使用的管理对注塑产品的成本有很大影响，顺景系统具有完整的水口料管理方案，对企业成本控制严谨到位。  查看详情 3C电子ERP系统 电子行业技术发展迅速，产品的更新换代也快，引起产品BOM变更频繁，顺景ERP的BOM批量变更功能能快速准确进行物料变更，并且详细记录变更的内容以及与以前BOM版本的差别比较，很多物料也有替代使用需求，ERP的替代料功能支持完全替代、混批替代在生产计划，生产领料方面都有完整成熟方案支持，并能做不同供应商和不同批次的品质追溯。  查看详情 汽车配件安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 汽配行业的工厂，基本都是跟汽车整厂进行配套生产，一般都采取滚动预测的模式进行备料和生产，顺景ERP系统有滚动FORECAST模式，支持先备料和生产，然后在接到客户订单后再进行快速的送货，并且订单会和销售预测进行勾稽核销，同时系统还支持物料批次管理，能做到完整的产品品质的异常追溯功能。  查看详情 机械制造ERP系统 机械装备行业，物料种类繁多，生产周期长，现在一般都进行模组化设计，对于根据标准机型衍生的特殊机型，顺景ERP系统可以基于标准机型BOM进行复制后的快速定制，同时机械行业大多存在分期收款的要求，根据生产进度进行多期收款的设置和到期催款的预警，顺景ERP也支持详细的售后服务的安装、维修、保养等功能。  查看详情 照明行业安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 照明灯饰行业，物料分为多个不同种类，包括发光光源、电线电源、金属支架、水晶配件、金属配件、防护包材等非常多不同属性的材料加工、组装而成，所以生产计划的物料需求计算、厂内外发的物料管理、仓库的物料库存管理、上线组装前的物料齐套作业等成为灯饰行业管理的重中之重，顺景生产的核心就是以计划为驱动，物料管理为基础的制造业ERP系统。  查看详情 家用电器ERP系统 家用电器行业已经发展成为国内支柱产业，也越来越智能化，一般通过注塑或者金属外壳，内部功能组件和电子控制几个部分组成，在生产制造业环节，对生产计划的物料需求、材料采购交期、外发加工周期、厂内部件生产的合理安排尤为重要，对销售渠道的管理要求也越来越高，顺景ERP既支持传统销售模式的订单，也支持电子商务的订单等多销售渠道的管理。  查看详情 医疗器械安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 医疗器械是生命健康产业重要的子领域之一，是精密制造与精准医疗渗透、单点创新与集成创新融合的典型代表。由于医疗器械对生命健康的影响至关重要，所以在产品研发、实验、制造各环节的管控要求都非常高，顺景ERP支持单品的序列号管理，生产过程中的每一种物料都能支持批号和序列号的收发，从根本上保证了品质异常的追溯。  查看详情 化工行业ERP系统 化工行业的配方管理是其核心机密，同时对生产过程中的压力、温度等参数都要求要有详尽的记录，顺景ERP支持物料、产品BOM配方等核心物料的加密管理，从系统层面就杜绝了配方泄密的问题，同时也会从机器直接采集其生产的相关参数记录进ERP系统，并且对化工产品的不同生产批次，从批号的产生规则，分批号入库，分批号出库，分批号标识，分批号盘点的全批号管理流程，对于保质期到期前的预警提醒等功能。  查看详情 玩具行业安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 玩具行业一般有模型玩具和毛绒玩具之分，模型玩具有电子控制部分、五金机械部分和注塑外壳组装而成，产品零部件较多，同时兼具电子、五金、塑胶等行业特性，BOM表的准确、完整、及时是关键。毛绒玩具，其布料的裁料、部件的针车、内外衬粘贴、定型包装是其主要特征，由于玩具使用对象为儿童，对材料的环保性和安全性要求较高，顺景系统都有材料认证管理，同时对个人计件、集体计件和工时的薪资完整核算体系。  查看详情 机器人ERP系统 机器人行业是国内工业4.0的重要发展行业，多为客制化订单，边研发边调试边生产，一般都采取项目式生产，并且根据项目进度进行分期收款和成本核算，顺景ERP的订单BOM配置功能很完整的适合这种生产模式，系统形成完整的生产和改动记录，并作为后续产品迭代改进和售后服务的参考依据。  查看详情 家具行业安博网页版-安博（中国）官方 家具行业本属于传统大批量生产的行业，但是由于现代人对品质生活的追求，定制化程度越来越高，这就对家具行业的生产要求也越来越高，顺景ERP系统支持与前端的产品模型设计的工具直接对接，快速地生成物料编码、产品BOM，车间根据产品BOM规格的要求进行快速的生产，同时对生产过程中的部件进行条码标识和快速扫描采集生产进度，大大支持了个性化定制的生产模式。  查看详情 成功案例 title: Prineville Swim Team | LIFE IS BETTER WHEN YOU ARE SWIMMING!
text: Prineville Swim Team | LIFE IS BETTER WHEN YOU ARE SWIMMING! 541-447-7546 prinevilleswimteam@gmail.com Select Page PRINEVILLE SWIM TEAM (PST) Pool: 399 NE Garner Street Mail: PO Box 511 Prineville, OR 97754 REGISTRATION FOR THE 2026 SWIM SEASON IS NOW CLOSED COME CHEER ON OUR SWIMMERS AT OUR HOME MEET JUNE 19TH – 21ST! Register Now Halley Estes, Head Coach halleyestes23@gmail.com Assistant Coaches: Katie Catterson – Hannah Crockett Important Information for the 2026 Swim Season…. REGISTRATION FOR THE 2026 SWIM SEASON IS NOW CLOSED If you’re a returning swimmer, Click the Register Now button at the top of the screen to register for the 2026 swim season If you are a new swimmer, we recommend you attend one of our In-Person Registration events to learn more In Person Registration events will be held at the Prineville Pool: Wednesday, April 29th from 5:30 – 7:00 PM Saturday, May 16th from 1:00 – 3:00 PM All swimmers are required to register with USA Swimming as a seasonal swimmer. Parents are responsible for completing the registrion process with USA Swimming directly. This is required and must be completed prior to your swimmer getting in the water! If you have any questions, please reach out to us via email prinevilleswimteam@gmail.com or attend one of our in-person registration events Swim Team Practice is tenatively scheduled to start on Monday, May 26th (Day after Memorial Day). All swim practices will take place in the afternoons until school is out for the summer, then morning practices will begin (Practice times to be announced) Parent Information Ages 5 through 18 are eligible to join PST. After a two week trial period, swimmers must be able to swim the width of the pool or the coaches will notify the parent/guardian if the swimmer needs further swimming lessons prior to joining PST. Additional questions should be directed to the PST Board Members. Practices are held Monday through Friday (times vary by skill level). You will be notified of specific practice times within the first two weeks of the season. Swim practice usually starts mid-late May. Swim Fees: $300 for the season per swimmer. Families with more than one swimmer will receive a $25 discount for each additional child. Beginner swimmers may be allowed to swim for $250 at the coach’s discretion (Discounts not available for beginners). Fees will cover the following: PST Registration, Monthly dues, Splash fees for all scheduled meets (below) & Team Swimsuits. Fees can be paid as one lump sum or in three equal payments. Registration fees must be paid in full by June 1st in order for the swimmer to participate in any swim meet. Payment arrangements must be set up with the PST board prior to the season beginning. Scholarships may be available. (Limit one per family). You can find the PST Scholarship form here . This form must be filled out by the swimmer applying and given to a PST Board Member. 2026 Swim Meet Schedule The Dalles Invitational: June 12th – 14th PST – Prineville Invitational: June 19th – 21st Lakeview Lions Invitational: June 26th – 28th Pendleton Open: July 4th – 5th Lincoln City – PST Dual: July 10th Burns Hi-Desert Invitational: July 17th – 19th East Cascade District Finals – (Burns): July 24th – 26th Things to Take to a Swim Meet Team suit, goggles, cap (if needed) team sweatshirt. List of races entered Towels and sandals Sleeping bag, blankets, sweats or cover up for cold times Sunscreen and hat for hot times Lunch or spending money Snacks (granola, fruit, juices, cheese), lunch cooler Concession stands are usually available Overnight needs depending on accommodations Please label everything you bring to the swim meets, home or away! We are not responsible for lost or stolen items. Swim Meet Information All teams in the Cascade East District attend and help at all the meets. Parents from all teams will be asked to assist with timing. Most of the meets we attend are invitational meets where the host team invites those teams they want to participate. Meets run from Friday night through Sunday afternoon. We encourage all swimmers to attend all meets, but swimmers are only required to swim in one meet within the Cascade East District to qualify to swim at the finals. Swimmers can swim up to 6 individual events per meet plus relays. Age groups: In most cases, the age groups at swim meets are: 8 & under, 9-10, 11-12, 13-14 and 15-18 for both boys and girls. Relays events are 8 & under, 10 & under, 12 & under, 14 & under and 18 & under. Events: Swim meet events are in freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, butterfly, individual medleys and relays. The coach places swimmers in the events depending on ability and past performance times. Relay Times: The coach will decide upon members for freestyle and medley relays. It is not always feasible for a swimmer to swim within his/her age group when putting together relay teams. Please remember that the coach will do what is best for the team and not necessarily what you think is best for the individual. Please respect and support the coach’s decision. Officials: Officials include director, announcer, referee, starter, timer, stroke & turn judges, place judges and safety officer. PST will pay the registration fees that USS requires as a team expense. These volunteers provide a great service to our team and are a necessary part of the swim program. Disqualifications: Stroke and turn judges are at the sides of the pool during competition in each event. If a swimmer does a stroke/kick incorrectly and/or performs any other violation determined by OSI regulations, the swimmer will be disqualified from that event. Home Meets: As host team, we are responsible for planning and executing the entire meet. Volunteers will be needed for preparation, clean-up, concessions, food donations, and meet officials (timers, ribbons, clean-up, etc.) All parents are required to help during our home meet. Many workers make the job go much faster and we can all get done sooner. Thank you for your support!! Away Meets: Away meets run between Friday evening and Sunday afternoon. Many of the team families use tents or campers to camp out in the parks next to the pools. Others stay in motels or with friends and relatives. Please feel free to ask fellow parents for ideas on where to stay in each town. Designed by Elegant Themes | Powered by WordPress

title: Richmond Sailfish - Richmond Swims
text: Richmond Sailfish - Richmond Swims Richmond Swims Swim Teams/Groups Richmond Sailfish Richmond Plunge Masters (RPM) Richmond Open Water Events Keller Cove Swim Masters Swim Clinics Lessons Private Lessons Adult – Beginning Lap Swim (Bridge to Masters) Adult – Learn to Swim (Swimming Saves Lives) Kids – Pre-Swim Team Kids – Take The Plunge Pool practices are temporarily suspended due to COVID-19. Please see our COVID-19 page for information about our open water and dryland workouts. --> Richmond Sailfish Mission Statement The mission of the Richmond Sailfish is to encourage and empower young people to develop to their fullest potential as athletes, individuals, and role models in their community through participation program especially aims to provide inner-city youth throughout Richmond with an opportunity to develop swimming skills, character and self-discipline in a supportive environment that fosters personal improvement. Our team offers all swimmers the chance to excel by maintaining small group sizes to ensure each swimmer plenty of personal attention from their coach. With monthly competitions and other participate on our team in a safe environment while learning a necessary life skill. Schedule and Registration Practices are currently Mon-Fri from 4-6pm. We are using TeamUp to manage our registration and payments. This service has a very flexible and user-friendly method of managing memberships for families. This help article does a great job of explaining how the system works. Follow this link to create or manage your account or membership. All returning Sailfish swimmers must submit their current year USA swimming athlete registration form, as this provides our team’s liability insurance. Below is the link to register online with Pacific Swimming. If you have any questions about this registration process, including questions about outreach registration please talk to the Head Coach before or after practice or reach out via email . Standard registration for 2027: CLICK HERE Coached Workout Schedule Sailfish coached pool workouts at the Plunge are year round. The workouts will be held Monday through Friday from 4:00 to 6:00 pm. Duration of workout will depend on age and ability of swimmer Guppy Group: 4:00-4:50pm Mon-Fri Minnow Group: 4:45-6:00pm Mon-Fri Sailfish Group: 4:00-6:00pm Mon-Fri Basic Swimming Skills Needed to Join Youth are not required to be proficient swimmers to join the Sailfish, but some basic water skills are needed. To be “Swim Team Ready”, children should be able to: Float like an airplane or jellyfish (without moving) for 5-10 seconds with their face in the water. Propel themselves by kicking for about 20 feet and should be able to take a few bites of air, using a dog paddle without touching the bottom of the pool. Be comfortable blowing bubbles in the water. Jump into the deep end of a pool and comfortably swim over to the side. Move their arms and kick in a freestyle (big arms) and backstroke – although it doesn’t have to look pretty. Coordinate their arms to their strong kick with instruction. Either open their eyes under water or be comfortable with goggles. Be happy in the pool without a parent. For the younger swimmers we will first be teaching how to side breathe during freestyle, which is critical as it develops proper form and technique. Once they get stronger and develop a nice backstroke. Introduction to Butterfly and Breaststroke as well as learning and practicing turns and dives will also help the swimmers gain a strong understanding of competitive swimming. Older swimmers will spend more practice time focusing on specific stroke technique work, cardiovascular training, and race strategy, with longer practice times and an increase in intensity. Registration and Fees USA Registration: Everyone is required to register with USA Swimming and pay annual dues, which cover insurance and subscription to Swimming World Magazine. Swimmers should carry their cards with them at swim meets or other USA Swimming events as they may be required to show it. (See above for USA Swimming links.) Sailfish Swimming Fees: Swimming fees cover pool rental costs, coach’s salary, equipment and various overhead expenses for the Sailfish. Dues are payable in full at the beginning of each month. MONTHLY DUES FOR FULL TIME SWIMMERS Guppy group – $95/swimmer Minnow group – $100/swimmer Sailfish group – $110/swimmer Scholarship Families – $65/swimmer See the information above about registration via TeamUp. Membership payments are also processed via this system. Alternately, fees can be paid by check made out to “Richmond Swims”, and given to the Coach or sent to the attention of the Club Registrar at P.O. Box 70952, Richmond, CA 94807. Team Gear For team swim suit and Parka orders click on this link: RICHMOND SAILFISH 14 SafeSport Information Safe sport club coordinator: John Schonder To deal with a Safe Sport concern, contact USA Swimming at (719) 866-4578. Contact the U.S. Center for Safe Sport to make a report. Call (720) 524-5640 or use the online reporting form or find more information at http://www.uscenterforsafesport.org/ Additional SafeSport resources can be found here Coaches Head Coach John Schonder The Head Coach is John Schonder. John grew up and began his swimming career in Reno, Nevada. He swam competitively through high school and into college. He spent several years teaching of Reno Parks and Recreation Aquatics Department and the Reno Aquatics Club from 1995 through 2000. He was Head Coach for the Holy Names High School (Oakland) swim team from 2005 Coach and Executive Director of the Oakland Barracudas (age group and Masters swimming teams) from March 2007 until December 2009. He is active on the Pacific Swimming Diversity and swimming more accessible to communities that have traditionally not had access to swimming. John holds a Level II Certification with the American Swimming Coaches Association (ASCA), is Professional Trainer through Aerobics and Fitness Association of America. Assistant Coach Kaitlin Harris Kaitlin started swimming with the Richmond Sailfish in 2010, the inaugural year. She continued to swim and compete up until high school where she was a Varsity Swimmer all four years. Specializing in middle distance freestyle (200 free, 500 free), she is a very versatile swimmer, able to swim all the high school events. Kaitlin is a Red Cross Certified Lifeguard, and worked previously at the Richmond Plunge/Swim Center as well as the El Cerrito pool as a lifeguard and swim instructor. She is also a primary instructor in the Take the Plunge community swim lesson program. Kaitlin started coaching the Guppy and Minnow group in Fall of 2018, and is a certified USA Swimming coach. Assistant Coach Jose Luis Albarran Jose started swimming with the Richmond Sailfish in 2010 as one of the team’s first 44 swimmers. During his 8 years with the team he competed at regional meets, volunteered to teach swim lessons to local Richmond youth, and was one of two first team captains. He is currently a lifeguard with the City of Richmond, and is in school to receive his EMT certification with plans to attend Fire fighter academy. For More Information If you are interested in learning more about Richmond Sailfish and/or would like to be included on an email list for updated information please contact Coach John Schonder at richmondswims@gmail.com ONLINE STORE NOW OPEN! text: Schofield Sharks Swim Club - Home Schofield Sharks Swim Club Contact Us Home Team Info & Pictures Coaches Calendar of events Team Records Groups and Practices Team Apparel and Equipment Photos FAQ Pools > Policies How to Join Transfer Links Volunteering Contact Us May 8, 2024 GOODBYE SHARKS! ​ ~This is an update on the Schofield Sharks Swim Team~ Due to the COVID19 shutdown in 2020 the team was unable to recover and is no longer active. Richardson Pool is beginning swim lessons this year to help children who are interested in swimming get prepared to try out for other swim teams on the island of Oahu. If interested please contact Mike Bell the manager of Richardson Pool at MWR Army Aquatics . This website will remain up as a reminder of the history and pride the Schofield Sharks stood for during the years of 1955-2020. To the left is a picture of our very own Coach Blake being inducted into the Hawai'i Swimming Hall of Fame in 2022. Thank you Coach Blake for being there for so many swimmers over the years....GO SHARKS!!! Schofield Sharks Swim Club 40th Anniversary Schofield Sharks Team History Hawaiian Swimming Active Teams ​​The Schofield Sharks Swim Club is a competitive swim team for children ages 6 to 18. Since 1955 we have been dedicated to teaching competitive swimming skills and proper stroke technique in a fun yet disciplined team environment. The team practices year-round at Richardson Pool, located on Schofield Barracks, on the island of Oahu, Hawaii. We are the second oldest swim club in the State of Hawaii. Sharks Swim Team c/o Richardson Pool, ​1028 KoleKole Ave. Building 578, Schofield Barracks, Hi 96857 (808) 787-4090 ​(Richardson Pool is located directly behind Division Headquarters) ​ *** Attention *** Do you have extensive water experience? text: San Diego Seaport Aquatics Home Get Connected Facebook Instagram Sign in Homepage Join Us Contact Us Trying Out Register with SDSA About The SDSA Creed USA Swimming Safe Sport Partnership Coaches Programs Registration & Fees 2026 Practice Schedule Team Calendar Events Team Records Safe Sport Billing & General Policies Privacy Policy Anchor Booster Club View Upcoming Events Join the Team Sea to Desert Swim Association Locations Brian Bent Memorial Complex Coronado, CA Mesa College Pool San Diego, CA El Centro Aquatic Center El Centro, CA Meet Your Future Crew Schedule a Tryout Meet the Coaches Swim Programs for all Ages and Abilities We offer skill-specific training for all of our athletes geared towards challenging and developing each individual. Please contact us to schedule a tryout or request more information. Ask a Question Age Group PURPLE (6-week option) Learn the interaction between the water and how your body moves in it with less committment. This group focuses on strong, kick driven strokes. Read More >> Age Group PURPLE (12-unders monthly) Further your stroke technique and develop new skills to progess your training. Kicking and endurance are emphasized here. Read More >> Age Group GOLD (Ages 10-14) Learn about racing strategy, increase your aerobic training, build strength, power and endurance in the water. Read More >> Senior Development (Ages 13+) This group requires strong knowledge of stroke mechanics and training modalities. It's a great addition to high school practice. Read More >> Senior Elite (Ages 13+) This is our highest level group. Get ready to commit, have a driven attitude and work ethic. Gear up and meet your potential. Read More >> Swim Conditioning (Ages 10+) This group is for athletes who love swimming but don't want to fully commit. It's a condensed program that still helps you advance your skills and speed. Read More >> Tryout Information Tell us your swimming experience, goals and skills in the water. We will suggest the best group, and schedule a day for you to practice with the team. This will be your tryout! You may also request to do a 1:1 evaluation, but we encourage attending a training session so that you can meet the team. Schedule Tryout Our Partners Safe Sport Information To deal with a Safe Sport concern , contact USA Swimming at (719) 866-4578, or contact the U.S. Center for Safe Sport to make a report by calling 833-5US-SAFE(587-7233). You can also use the online reporting form . Pool deck moments Training, friendships, team events, and a whole lot of water. The Stingrays experience is bigger than a practice lane: swimmers learn, compete, celebrate, and grow up around a team that feels like family. About the team A South San Jose year-round swim team for swimmers who want to keep growing. We offer a transition from summer swimming to training and competing throughout the year. We are not just a swim team; we are a family, with activities that help families and swimmers bond with one another. Positive coaching, clear expectations, and a real team culture. South Valley Stingrays is located in South San Jose. Our mission is to create a positive and engaging environment where children can learn the sport of swimming while having fun. Every member of our staff has a passion for swimming and is on a mission to help swimmers discover their own passion for the sport. Coaches & hours Practice groups are primarily based on ability. Coach Jerry Head Coach Coach Jerry has more than 40 years of coaching experience across high school, club, and collegiate swimming. His background includes Pioneer, Valley Christian, and Santa Teresa high schools, as well as San Jose Aquatics, Valley Splash, and San Jose State University. During his career, he has coached three CCS champions. While coaching at San Jose State alongside Pablo Morales, he helped guide two swimmers to NCAA competition. He also coached two swimmers to the Olympic Trials level, including one who went on to represent her country at the Olympic Games. Link to Registration Page THE PURPOSE OF THE SEALS Seals Aquatics/Strawberry Seals exists to help children thrive as confident, fit and technically proficient swimmers. We nurture a life-long love of swimming by creating an environment where competition, team spirit, personal growth and a strong swim community flourish. We are a competitive swim team that participates in in USA Swimming, Pacific Swimming and the Marin Swim League competitions. Swimmers should have a goal of participating in competitions withing 1-2 years of joining the program. Since basic skills are not taught at practice, swimmers should have a strong foundation of swim lessons prior to joining the team. Swimmers joining at the Seal Pup, Ribbon Seal or Harbor Seal levels may need supplemental swim lessons to advance to the next group. Freestyle proficiency requires sideways breathing. Must be able to swim 25 yards unassisted without stopping. Must be confident and safe in deep water. Intermediate: Proficient in at least three competition strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and/or butterfly). Can maintain focus during basic interval sets 4 – 12 minutes in duration. Advanced: Proficient in all four competition strokes and competition turns. Can maintain focus during interval sets 12 - 40 minutes in duration. text: Barracuda Aquatic Club Toggle navigation Home About Us Times/Records Monthly Payments USA Registration Meet Registration Safe Sport MISSION STATEMENT: Our team is a year round competitive swim team offering high quality professional coaching and technique instruction for all ages and abilities. The goal of our team is to provide every member an opportunity to improve swimming skills and achieve success at his or her level of ability, as well as helping them to grow into better individuals throughout their lives. The Barracuda Aquatic Club is also committed to providing a safe and supportive environment for all participants. To do so we have athlete protection policies and guidelines in place under the SAFE SPORT tab of our website.
