text: eam, lists her as the third fastest in the event for the history of the team, and only 0.76 seconds within the team record. Regan had two additional swims in the consolation final heat, and they included the 100 IM (1:06.59), and 100 breaststroke (1:12.36). Blake Rogers has made a name for himself within the team, and within a relatively short period of time. Along with Regan, he too has made his first appearance at Far Westerns, earning second swims in two of his three events entered. Blake’s highest finish was 9 th in the 11-12 50 yard breaststroke where his time of 32.10 is the sixth fastest time posted on the team, and moves him to being the third fastest in the event for the history of the team. Blake also touched 13 th in the 100 breaststroke, moving up two places from his seeding from the preliminary heats where he posted his lifetime best of 1:11.26. ALEXA WONG RESETS TEAM RECORD AT SMOC Four TNT swimmers traveled to Mission Viejo to compete in the 2022 Swim Meet of Champions, which has had a history of attracting international Olympic-level athletes, and had served at one time as the Olympic-Send-Off meet. This year our TNT Senior Team was well represented by four athlete who included Visalia’s Ella Bettencourt , along with Ava Olson, Alexa Wong and Bryan Wong . All four swimmers earned final swims at the meet, and scored in no less than two events. Performances in finals were led by long-time veteran too the meet, Bryan Wong , who scored in all four of his events, and having the highest finish of 3 rd in the 400 IM (4:39.90), and then following it with a 6 th place finish in the 200 IM (2:11.69). He also touched 12 th in the 200 breaststroke (2:27.88), and 14 th in the 100 breaststroke (1:07.58). Ella Bettencourt was our next highest finisher as she touched 6 th in the 50 meter backstroke (30.98), and 7 th in the 100backstroke (1:06.61) posting lifetime best times in all three events she entered. Next to Bryan, Alexa Wong had the next highest number of finals at three. Her highest finish being 5 th place in the 400 IM where her time of5:05.07 was an improvement to her previous team record of 5:08.50 set in La Mirada a couple of months earlier. Alexa swam twice under her re-existing record. She also touched 8 th in the 400 free (4:30.57), and 10 th in the 200 IM (2:25.09), and, along with Ella, was our only other athlete who improved 100% of her times. Ava Olson was our remaining finalist as she touched 7 th in the 400 free (4:30.53), and 14 th in the 200 free (2:09.05), and improving times in both of those events. PORTERVILLE’S REGAN HILDRETH FINALS AT SWAGR The Southwest Age Group Regional Championships, SWAGR for short, is a swim meet established several years ago as an alternative to the more competitive Far Western Championships, and structures events in single-age categories, opposed to age groups. The meet alternates between hosts of Clovis with teams in the Sierra-Nevada section just north of Central California Swimming. This year, the meet took place during the last weekend of March, and four TNT swimmers participated at the Clovis North complex. Of the four, Porterville’s Regan Hildreth was our sole scoring athlete as she posted championship swims in three of her seven events. Her highest place was a 6 th place finish in the 12-year old 50 yard breaststroke with a time of 33.58, followed by a 7 th place finish in the 200 breaststroke after posting a lifetime best by well over two seconds (2:40.09) in the preliminary heats. Swimmers in the top 10 places from the preliminary heats advanced to finals, and as a true breaststroker, Regan’s remaining breaststroke event also earned a championship swim. Her 100 breaststroke time of 1:14.79 touched 10 th in the event. Regan also posted a team’s All-Time Top-100 time in the 100 IM. Two other swimmers posted times among our team’s All-Time Top-100 rankings, and they included Danny Rodriguez who posted times in both the 50 and 100 freestyle events for the 13-14 age division, and Blake Rogers who posted All-Time Top-100 times in the 50 free, 100 free, 50 breaststroke and 100 breaststroke events, all in 11-12 boys division. Congratulations to all swimmers, including Isaak Ensz who, at 67%, posted the highest improvement percentage among the team. WONG, WONG AND OLSON FINAL AT SPRING SECTIONALS The TNT Spring Sectional Team for this year was composed of eight TNT swimmers representing towns of Coalinga, Visalia, Hanford, and Tulare who competed over the first weekend of March in Carlsbad, California. Three swimmers of our team performed well enough in the preliminary heats to earn a second swim in one of two final heats for their respective events. Representation in finals, and team point accumulation from individual events, was led by Bryan Wong who earned second swims in four of his six events, and posted a championship final swim in the 400 IM where his 3:56.95 touched fast enough for a bronze medal finish in the event. His swim was also a new team record, improving from his previous record of 3:59.45 set in December 2020 during the midst of the pandemic. His new record currently stands as the 40 th fastest nationally for male swimmers of age 17. Bryan also earned a second swim in the 200 breaststroke event with a time of 2:02.04 that finished 12 th in the event. His time once again fell under a record that was previously his at a 2:02.26 set this past December at Junior Nationals in Texas. Bryan went under his previous record during both swims (prelims and finals). His new record currently ranks 49 th nationally among male swimmers at his age. His other events that earned a swim in finals included the 200 IM (18 th , 1:52.69), and the 100 breaststroke (13 th , 56.14). Our next swimmer who earned a second swim was Ava Olson who swam a 4:24.55 in the 400 IM event, posting a lifetime best, and finished 14 th . Finally, Alexa Wong touched 28 th in the 200 fly after posting a lifetime best of 2:04.24 in the preliminary heats, and swimming under arguably one of the longest standing records what was established by Lynnie North as a 2:04.34 back in 1993 during a swim meet in the Fig Garde Racquet Club swimming pool. Alexa’s new team record currently ranks 45 th in the nation for girls at age 15. Besides the brother-sister duo of Bryan and Alexa Wong, Michelle Murphy also re-established team records, and she did this in two of her four events, while also being our youngest swimmer competing in Sectionals at fourteen years old. Michelle first posted a time of 5:04.20 in the 500 freestyle, which was nearly a 15-second improvement, and swam under Ava Olson’s previous team record of 5:04.98 set at the same meet two years earlier in 2020. Michelle’s new record stands as the 76 th fastest nationally for girls at age 14. Her second record was in the 200 freestyle, where she posted a time of 1:54.63 in the event, which slid under the previous record set by Samantha Goates in 2004 as a 1:54.71. Michelle’s new record stands at the 153 rd spot nationally for girls at the same age. Two of our swimmers improved 100% of their times, and these included Kate Geiger who trains out of Visalia, and Addison Mccullough . All eight TNT swimmers competing at Sectionals posted times in our team’s All Time Top-100 list, and they included Ella Bettencourt , and Gage Price . 3 TEAM RECORDS FALL AT JUANITA ALLINGTON MEMORIAL MEET The Juanita Allington Memorial swim meet is a local senior-level swim meet which our team has historically used as an entry-level senior experience for our developing swimmers. In past years, this meet provided our 12-under athletes exposure in competing in events with swimmers irrespective of age. For 2022, TNT had ten swimmers, all fourteen years and older, compete at the meet in Clovis, and three of our swimmers came away as event champions in their respective events. Fifteen-year-old Alexa Wong led the group by wining the time-based final 1000 freestyle (10:11.99), and also took home the gold in the 400 IM (4:24.34). Consequently, both events became new team records where her 1000 freestyle slid under Ava Olson’s previous record of 10:12.78 set this past November at the Kevin Perry meet. Alexa’s new record now stands as the 13 th fastest in the nation for girls at age 15. Her second record updates a longer standing time of 4:27.75 that was set in 2007 at the Winter Invite in Southern California, and set by Megan Eppler who went on to swim for the University of Kentucky. Alexa’s new record lands among the top 26 times nationally for girls her age. Ava Olson was the event champion in the 1650 freestyle event, and our other individual with a team record-breaking performance, and she did this with a time of 17:06.49 in the 1650 freestyle event, swapping records with Alexa by going under the previous mark of 17:39.74 that was set earlier in the month. Ava’s time stands as the 30 th fastest in the nation for girls at age 16. Our remaining event champion was Bryan Wong who won the 200 breaststroke with a time of 2:03.14. Other swimmers who finished in the top-16 included: Ella Bettencourt (5 th -50 free), Addison Mccullough (7 th -200 breast), Michelle Murphy (8 th -400 IM), Amy Murphy (10 th -100 breaststroke). SIX NAMED CCS SWIMMER OF THE YEAR FOR TNT AT JOs Thirty-two TNT swimmers competed at the 2022 Central California Swimming Short Course Junior Olympic Championships over the third weekend of February, and took the team to a sixth-place finish with a total of 1,185 points which was behind Bakersfield’s 1,416 fifth place, and just ahead of Fresno Dolphin’s at 1,161.5 points. There were 26 teams that scored at the meet that hosted a total of 28 teams representing regions throughout California and Nevada. Only one Central California Swimming team was among the top four scoring teams: Clovis (4025.5 points), Irvine (3164.5), Las Vegas (1808.5) and PUMA (1533). The team’s total point accumulation was led by Porterville’s Regan Hildreth who accumulated 113 points while earning a second swim in all seven individual events entered in the 11-12 girl’s division, and becoming the event champion in the 11-12 200 breaststroke event after improving over 14 seconds to a time of 2:40.87. Our next highest point getter was 11 year old Logan Huckabay (109 points), followed by our remining finalists who included: Zach Walker (94 points), Blake Rogers (94), Lexi Krigbaum (85), Hannah Beer (83), Mia Buller (79), Nathan Boudreaux (56), Josh Wee (54), Blake Sifton (54), Marisol Alvarez (52), Lance Walker (50), Danny Rodriguez (24), Gabriela Dutra (23), Tarrin Nelms (21), Reece Phillips (21), Canyon Johnson (19), Kody Kevorkian (15), Ivan Rodriguez (11), Ada Maher (11), Morgan Darpli (9), Josephine Batres (7), Isaak Ensz (7), Hayden Cardoza (7), and Emma Taylor (7). Regan Hildreth was among five TNT swimmers who were event champions in one or more events, and the group was led by eight-year-old Zack Walker who won three of his seven events by winning the 8-under 100 free (1:18.77), 50 back (42.32), and 50 freestyle (36.77) events. Twelve-year-old Blake Rogers took home the gold in both the 50 free (25.50) and 50 breaststroke (32.61) events. Our remaining two event champions included Lexi Krigbaum who won the 8-under 100 IM (1:34.03), and sixteen-year-old Mia Buller who won the 15-18 500 freestyle event with a lifetime best of 5:25.33. Thirteen swimmers improved 100% of their events while at the meet. Congratulations go to: Marisol Alvarez, Morgan Darpli, Logan Huckabay, Kody Kevorkian, Lexi Krigbaum, Ada Maher, Addison Mccullough, Tarrin Nelms, Reece Phillips, Danny Rodriguez, Ivan Rodriguez, Blake Rogers, and Lance Walker . Annually, during the short course Junior Olympic Championships, Central California Swimming recognizes the top male and top female swimmer at individual ages from 9 to 16, and the 17-18 age group based on ranking performance (Top-5 CCS and national) in nationally recognized events during the previous year’s performance. This year, six TNT swimmers were recognized as the Swimmer the Year for their respective ages this past year, and they include: Logan Huckabay (age 10 boys), Michelle Murphy (age 13 girls), Alexa Wong (age 14 girls), Ava Olson (age 15 girls), Bryan Wong (age 16 boys), and Danielle Albright (age 17-18 girls). ALEXA WONG SETS TEAM RECORD AT BC CHAMPIONSHIPS At a swim meet typically geared towards providing opportunity for swimmers to achieve Junior Olympic time standards, fifteen-year-old Alexa Wong took the opportunity to swim the 1650-yard freestyle (i.e. “mile”) for the very first time, and in doing so, set a new team record with a time of 17:39.74, which was well under the 15-18 record of 17:45.35 that was set by Katelyn Herrera at Sectionals in 2014. Alexa’s new team record also falls under the team’s Senior record, since her time also slid under Danielle Albright’s 13-14 age group record of 17:40.29 set at a Clovis meet in 2016. Alexa’s time currently stands as the 69 th fastest nationally for girls at age15. Approximately 75 TNT swimmers competed at the BC Championships held in Visalia over the first weekend of February, in preparation of the Junior Olympics will occurs two weeks out. A level of meet that does not typically result in rankings among our all-time top-100 list, four swimmers did just that. A pair of our sixteen-year-old female swimmers ( Marison Avlarez and Mia Buller ) braved the distance event of the 1000 freestyle, posting times of 12:47.05 and 11:51.51 respectively, ranked in the 15-over list, while 12-year-old Nathan Boudreaux swam the 200-breaststroke event for the first time, and posted a Top-100 ranking in the 11-12 boys division with his time of 2:43.45 right out of the shoot. Eleven-year-old Regan Hildreth took on one of the most difficult races for the first time, and posted a ranking in the 11-12 girls 400 IM with a time of 5:27.26 while still on the bottom of the age division. When considering only those events previously recorded with the team in distances 50 yards or longer, congratulations to the following swimmers who improved 100% of their times: Hannah Beer (age 8), Nathan Boudreaux (12), Mia Buller (16), Aubree Carlock (11), Brody Diaz (9), Gabriela Dutra (15), Logan Hildreth (15), Regan Hildreth (11), Isabella Klawitter (16), Makenzie Krum (9), Willa Lasse (8), Marlee Lininger (13), Ada Maher (8), Jett Mahoney (6), Benita Marshall (9), Noa Martin (9), Makayla McGuire (14), Casey Minnig (12), Sophie Nelsen (14), Tyson Phillips (13), Danny Rodriguez (14), Payton Rose (12), Brooke Seliskar (9), Trig Seliskar (12), Jacquene Taylor (9), Ryker Thornton (10), and Adelyn Watkins . Congratulations also go to the many swimmers who posted new times with the team in events 50 yards or longer. They include: Marisol Alvarez, Nya Awbrey, Josephine Batres, Hannah Beer, Nathan Boudreaux, Mia Buller, McKenzie Chavez, Faith Contreras, Jayce DeRuiter, Sophie Ericson, Mya Figallo, Agusting Gonzalez, Logan Hildreth, Regan Hildreth, Kody Kevorkian, Makayla McGuire, Ayla Morgan, Sophie Nelson, Caleb Newman, Evelynn Newman, Kelechi Nnadi, Ayane Rivello, Danny Rodriguez, Payton Rose, Jacqueline Taylor, Lia Tena, Allison Tos, Elsy Witt, Alexa Wong, than Zuniga and Owen Zuniga. VISALIA’S ELLA BETTENCOURT TOUCHES 2nd AT FRESNO SENIOR MEET A total of 28 TNT swimmers competed at the Fresno Dolphins Senior meet which provided exposure to a trials and finals formatted swim meet for not only our current senior-level swimmers, but also to our up-and-coming age group swimmers who gain experience from competing in a senior formatted meet, that offers two swims if qualifying for a final. Half of our swimmers earned a spot in one of three final heats, and these fourteen finalists included: Ella Bettencourt (age 16; swimming finals in 1), Emma Bettencourt (16; with 2 finals), Drew Black (15; 2), Mia Buller (16; 2), Hayden Cardoza (12; 2), Gabriela Dutra (15; 3), Isaak Ensz (11; 2), Koen Ensz (13; 3), Kody Kevorkian (17; 3), Rylee Medina (13; 1), Ayla Morgan (14; 1), Amy Murphy (16; 4), Ivan Rodriguez (13; 6), and Blake Sifton (17; 1). Our top finisher was Visalia’s 16-year old Ella Bettencourt who touched 2 nd in the 200 IM with at time of 2:15.24, after a 5 th place seed from the preliminary heats. Ella is one of our senior swimmers who have qualified for, and competed in, both high-level age group competitions, and senior-level meets, that take place both in state, and out of state. Ella has established herself early on by being the third fastest 50 freestyler in the history of our team for the 13-14 girls division. Other championship, top-8, finishes came from: Drew Black (7 th in the 100 fly and 8 th in the 100 breaststroke), Kody Kevorkian (7 th in the 100 breaststroke), Amy Murphy (4 th in the 200 breaststroke and 7 th in the 100 breaststroke), Ivan Rodriguez (6 th in the 100 backstroke), and Blake Sifton (7 th in the 100 free). Three swimmers posted times in the team’s all-time top 100 list, and these included Nathan Boudreaux (11-12 boys 50 & 100 breaststroke), Regan Hildreth (11-12 girls 50 &O 200 breaststroke), and Blake Rogers (11-12 boys 50 freestyle). Our emphasis is on stroke development, technique, conditioning, goal-setting, physical fitness and race strategies. Our professional coaches motivate all athletes to grow and improve in a fun and positive learning environment. We are a United States Swimming (USAS) team and all swimmers must become USAS members upon joining. All new swimmers are evaluated prior to joining the team to ensure they are placed in the best training group for them based on their age, skill level, and experience. We conduct evaluations on a regular basis. Please check the team web site banner for the next evaluation day/time! We are a club built by coaching professionals, with training groups for every stage of an athlete's development: the beginner learning all four strokes, the eleven-year-old chasing a first Far Western cut, the high schooler racing at Junior Nationals, and the professional training for a World Championship team. Our mission is to provide a positive, challenging and inclusive environment where athletes of all levels can grow. Success in the pool begins with a commitment to the daily process: showing up consistently, training with intention and taking on new challenges. Winning with Alto is a product of enthusiasm, hard work and fun. Where do you start? Competitive Team Year-round USA Swimming training in three programs: Age Group for 12 and under, Senior Prep for 13 and over, and our Senior, National and Professional groups. Placement is by tryout. title: B Town Brazadas Swim Club: Bakersfield Swim Programs
text: B Town Brazadas Swim Club: Bakersfield Swim Programs Teams Swim Team Summer Rec Team Masters Private Coaching Programs Swim League Stroke School Swim School Private Lessons Lap Swim Schedules Swim Team Practices Swim Team Meets Masters Team Practices Lap Swim About Our Story Staff Facilities Careers Contact Shop REGISTER HERE Teams Swim Team Summer Rec Team Masters Private Coaching Programs Swim League Stroke School Swim School Private Lessons Lap Swim Schedules Swim Team Practices Swim Team Meets Masters Team Practices Lap Swim About Our Story Staff Facilities Careers Contact Shop B-Town Brazadas Swim Club With every stroke, challenge, and teammate, we nurture personal growth and community connection. Why Join Our Swim Club? Brazadas is a welcoming swim community for athletes of all ages and abilities. Our programs help swimmers get in the water, stay active, build confidence, and improve their skills in a supportive environment. We offer swim lessons for a range of abilities, a youth swim league focused on teamwork and skill development, year-round competitive teams, Brazadas Masters for adults, and lap swimming. ﻿ Some programs, including swim lessons and the swim league, are open to non-members. Brazadas membership is required for the year-round team, Masters, and lap swim. Members also receive discounts on eligible programs and complimentary access to lap swim. BENEFITS OF JOINING: Get Fit Be Water Safe Learn New Skills Build Confidence Make Friends Enjoy a Lifelong Sport Have Fun! Join Bakersfield’s best swim club at the East Side Aquatic Center. Welcome to our swim club Get Ready to Dive In We're excited to welcome you to Brazadas Swim Club! Register today and become part of a community that builds skills, confidence, and a lifelong love of swimming. Register Now Contact Us ﻿ Our Programs Swim Programs for Everyone Our programs foster a supportive and safe environment where athletes of all ages can develop both as swimmers and individuals. Led by expert coaches in our state-of-the-art facility, we ensure each participant's needs are met at every stage of their swimming journey. YEAR ROUND Brazadas Swim Team For swimmers 6 to 18 who want to take it to the next level with expert coaching and stroke development. Plus the opportunity to compete in local, regional and national meets. Focus is on technique, endurance, and teamwork. Learn More FALL - WINTER - SPRING - SUMMER Brazadas Swim League For swimmers ages 6–18 who want to stay active, build endurance, and improve their skills through structured swim training. Focus is on fitness, technique, and confidence in the water. Learn More Spring, summer, & fall Brazadas Swim School From beginner to advanced, our certified instructors provide lessons for ages 3 to 18 years old. We focus on water safety, stroke technique, and building confidence in the water. Small class sizes ensure personalized attention. Learn More YEAR ROUND Brazadas Masters For adults of every skill level – from those who swim for fitness to retired competitors who still love to race! Our program gives swimmers the chance to be challenged, learn new skills, and refine their technique in a team environment. Learn More YEAR ROUND Private Swim Lessons One-on-one coaching to help swimmers master essential skills and refine their technique. Also good for children who prefer one-on-one attention over a group setting. Learn More About B-Town Brazadas Swim Club our story B-Town Brazadas Swim Club was founded by local residents who wanted to bring the benefits of swimming to the children of Bakersfield. We are a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization dedicated to providing accessible and affordable programs for all. LEARN MORE OUR FACILITIES The East Side Aquatic Center Bakersfield's newest pool — the state-of-the-art East Side Aquatic Center — is the proud home of the Brazadas. The Olympic-sized pool, located at Highland High School, provides swimmers with the perfect environment for training, learning, and competing. It’s always a great day to swim at Carpinteria Community Pool! Open year-round with an average water temperature of 80° (plus or minus 2 degrees). Address: 5305 Carpinteria Ave, Carpinteria, CA 93013 Phone: (805) 566-2417 Email: carppool@carpinteriaca.gov Important Note – Our payment processing company charges a 4% service fee for credit card payments. It will come through on your statement as an additional charge from your program charge. You can pay with check or cash in person at Carpinteria Community Pool if you wish but it must be done during business hours. We no longer accept American Express. We also do not accept Tap or Apple Pay. Register Here Registration: To sign up for aquatics memberships or programs, click the register button above. This was the motto of the club's former head coach, Matt Casto. He believed in it so much that he had it tattooed on his chest. Matt Casto believed every athlete had potential if they worked hard and NEVER SETTLED for less than their absolute best. His infectious enthusiasm for life and love for the sport inspired many young athletes until his sudden death from heart failure. EGAC is part of Matt's legacy. He loved this team and that love lives on in every race and in every athlete. Many of our swimmers, families, and coaches knew Matt personally. His impact is still felt throughout this club. text: Swim Team Make A Difference in Scott Valley-Join the Etna PAL Board. *KIDS * COPS*COMMUNITY* Home Programs Amateur Sports Explorers ClayBirds Swim Team RecSwim Events Skatepark About Become a Member Donate Our Mission About Us Join Our Team Volunteer Applications Volunteer Code of Conduct More Home Programs Amateur Sports Explorers ClayBirds Swim Team RecSwim Events Skatepark About Become a Member Donate Our Mission About Us Join Our Team Volunteer Applications Volunteer Code of Conduct Home Programs Amateur Sports Explorers ClayBirds Swim Team RecSwim Events Skatepark About Become a Member Donate Our Mission About Us Join Our Team Volunteer Applications Volunteer Code of Conduct SVST Information, Fees and Registrations Etna PAL Swim Team is a program run by the Etna Police Activities League, Inc. The team was established in the summer of 2000. We are known in the community by different names: Scott Valley Swim Team (SVST), Sharks , Etna PAL Swim Team. Let me explain, our team has been registered with USA Swimming since 2000 as Scott Valley Swim Team (SVST), our team mascot is "Sharks", and the team is financed, insured, and run through Etna Police Activities League (PAL). We are all the same, all inter-exchangeable, and all united! The Swim team is run through the help of a parent committee that is overseen and directed by the Etna PAL's Board of Directors. Participation: Etna PAL serves school age youth from the ages of 5-18. Can your child swim the length of the pool. (If the answer is no, please sign your child up for swim lessons through the City of Etna's Dotty Olson Community Pool .) Due to safety issues, child must be able to swim length of pool to be on the team. This will be evaluated by the coach. With the Swim Team Registration , you will also obtain 2024-2025 Etna PAL Membership if you have not already. These are separate fees (Due after passing the Swim Test): 2026-2027 Etna PAL Membership $30/youth (for those who are not current members) 2025 Swim Team Registration $100/youth USA Swim Registration/Fees will be obtained and paid for by the parent (you must have this in order to compete at meets) Swim Meet Registration/Fees will be obtained and paid for by the parent (you must do this for each meet attending) Our Sponsors Register Now! Form covers both PAL Membership & Swim Team Registration! What is the main goal of Etna PAL's Swim Team? Etna PAL's Swim Team is a competitive Swim Team, meaning we practice and train to compete at Swim meets as a team. Do we have to go to meets in order to be on the Swim Team? Etna PAL's Swim Team is a competitive Swim Team, meaning we practice and train to compete at Swim meets as a team. Etna PAL has another program offered for those just wanting their child to be in the pool daily with a routine of exercise and group activities. Please check out our RecSwim. How is Etna PAL's Swim Team funded? Etna PAL's Swim Team is funded through your Swim Team Registration fee and donations from individuals, corporations, and grants from foundations. Please visit our website to learn more about how you can support our mission. SVST Downloads Etna PAL Shark's MAAPP (pdf) Download USA Swim Concussion-info-sheet (pdf) Download Etna PAL Shark's Bullying Policy (pdf) Download Swim Team Rules Come to practice prepared with: A cheerful attitude; Swimsuit; Goggles; Cap Towel; Water bottle; Warm clothes Be on time. Swimmers and parents please stay and help with putting in and taking out lane lines and cleaning up swim equipment at the end of practice. If you need to use the restroom, you must ask the coach you are working with for that day before you leave the pool area. Warming up in the showers is not allowed during practice unless the need is recognized and allowed by a coach. Show respect to coaches and fellow teammates. When the coaches are speaking, there is to be no additional talking or whispering going on. You will have a chance to ask questions or make comments after announcements in the mornings. No bad language ever is to be used. You represent the EPAL/Scott Valley Swim Team and what you say and how you act reflects back to the team. Come to practice "to practice". No goofing off or disrupting others who are working hard. Swimmers will receive one warning from the coaches and if that swimmer chooses to continue making poor behavior choices, they will call their parents to pick them up or be asked to leave practice for the day. If that swimmer leaves on his/her own, their parents will be called after practice to discuss what happened. Coaches are not responsible for swimmers once their practice is finished. They will not be staying at the pool to wait for their parents. Please be prompt in picking up your children and watch your children who are not in the pool. Swimmers are not allowed in the pool office unless a coach asks them to get something for them. Rules of the Deck: Only Coaching Staff and swimmers that are practicing at the time allowed. Swimmers are only allowed on deck when it is their practice time. No Parents on deck. Parents, please refrain from coaching your children when they are at practice. If you'd like to help coach, please ask the coach for permission. Your children are in good hands with a great coaching staff. The coaches work as a team to give your children the tools to be efficient swimmers. If you have any questions or concerns, please talk to us either before or after practice. Each swimmer will set a goal or goals as to what they would like to achieve during the swimming season. The coaches will provide the tools for that swimmer to help them achieve those goals. It is up to you as a swimmer to want to use the tools to get better. No one else can achieve the goals you set for you. Use practice etiquette when swimming with others. Swimmers will swim in a circular motion, counterclockwise in their lanes. The lane line will always be to the right of their bodies. The fastest swimmers go first in each lane. After the first swimmer leaves, the second swimmer must wait an appropriate distance as directed by their coach. If for some reason another swimmer catches up to you, they will touch your foot. When you reach the end of the lane you are to let them pass you and wait until they reach an appropriate distance. Always follow the posted pool rules. Never dive or jump into the practice pool unless instructed to do so by your coaches. Other swimmers could be under the water in the pool and you may injure them and yourself if you are not careful. Check the whiteboard at practice for announcements. If you have a question or problem about anything at all, please let us know. We will do our best to find the answer or resolve the problem. If your problems or questions are not resolved, please reach out to Alicia Pindell, Etna PAL's Director, at etnapdpal@gmail.com or (530) 598-9833. Eat healthy foods before and after practice to replace the calories you will use during practice. Team suits and caps need to be worn at swim meets. A team swim cap must be worn during race events too. We will have a great summer; we are glad you are part of the team! GO SHARKS!! title: Lost Coast Aquatics Foundation – Fundamental aquatic training for Humboldt County youth.
text: Lost Coast Aquatics Foundation – Fundamental aquatic training for Humboldt County youth. Skip to content About Water Polo Swim Division Lost Coast Aquatics Foundation Making space for our local youth in and out of the water. It’s our commitment to provide fundamental training in as many ways as possible. We deliver effective, efficient workouts in dry land, strength training, aquatic safety, and aquatic sports. Membership Focused Training The LoCo Aquatics staff will build and design their session curriculum around the strengths of our members while improving their weaknesses. Local Aquatics Facilities The Cal Poly Humboldt Aquatics Center will be host to several of our clinics. The Arcata Community Pool will host our Saturday evening practices and we are teaming up with The Club for Fitness for weekday practices. Supportive Community We have an incredible crew of local professionals stepping in to support our programming. Offering Membership & training opportunities in: Group & Private Swim Lessons @ The Club for Fitness Interested in having your child(ren) learn to swim or improve their stroke work? The Club for Fitness offers 4-week group lessons and private lessons throughout the year. Email the Aquatics Director for more information: aquatics@thecluboncentral.com LoCo Water Polo Practice Schedule TBD We are focusing on funding at the moment. Click the link below to join our email list. Get Started + Dryland and Chalk Talk + In-water Skills For All Ages + Competition Opportunities + Session Length TBD Stroke Clinics We will be offering monthly stroke, turn, and film review clinics at The Club for Fitness in McKinleyville. Clinic Signup We’re Back!! Almost… January 17, 2025 Water polo will be back in March for a 6-week session. The practices will start with a 15-minute dryland warmup before hopping in for 1-hour of in-water training. The 6-week session will be $75 to cover facility rental costs and can be paid in cash, check, or through Venmo: @lost_coast_aquatics. November Stroke Clinic October 10, 2024 Our November stroke clinic will be on Sunday, November 17th at The Club for Fitness in McKinleyville. The event will be split out into two or three sessions: 12U: New to sport/competition through emerging stroke and competitive mindset development / 9:30 to 10:30 p.m. 10 to 14-year olds: Competitive Swimmer / Proficient in all (4)… Read more : November Stroke Clinic Block PARTY!!! October 10, 2024 Lost Coast Aquatics has been approved to host USA Swimming Block Party meets!!! We are waiting for facility rental confirmation before posting our two sanctioned meet dates/location. Swim meet and clinic information updates will be posted on our website. If you’d like to join our email list or know someone that would, click here. Lost Coast Aquatics Foundation Youth Sports and Athlete Development It is the tradition of LoCo to challenge our student-athletes in a positive teaching and training environment in which members can develop a sense of self-esteem and pride through individual and team achievement. Blog at WordPress.com. Stay updated Follow along on our journey to growing the sport of Water Polo and increasing access to aquatics programing in Humboldt County. Our 2026 swim season has ended. MLST is a seasonal team that typically operates from mid-May through mid-August or early September, taking advantage of Mammoth Lakes’ limited warm-weather season. Swimming in a high-altitude outdoor pool surrounded by the Sierra Nevada is a unique experience, combining competitive swimming with beautiful alpine views. Information about the 2027 season , including registration, tryouts, fees, and practice schedules, will be available by March 2027 . If you have additional questions, please contact us . ``` Text Area Simple formatted text Why Swim Team? Swim lessons teach children how to be safe and comfortable in the water. Swim team helps them grow beyond the basics. Once a swimmer can swim across the pool independently, they may be ready to join the team. At MLST, swimmers learn all four competitive strokes, starts, turns, and swim meet skills while building endurance, confidence, and technique. Practices also include games, teamwork, friendships, and lots of time in the water. Being part of a team keeps kids motivated, active, and excited to improve throughout the summer. We can’t wait to see the Sharks back in the pool. Go Sharks! Have questions? Contact us for more information! title: Mountain Club
text: Mountain Club Skip to content Welcome to Mountain Club for Swimming Los Alamos, New Mexico mountainswimming@gmail.com Our Mission To provide an opportunity for all ages to engage in physical fitness, proper conditioning, and recreational activity under the environment of safe sport, particularly for children. To provide a safe and supportive environment for child protection in swimming. To provide an environment for participants to effectively learn swimming skills and compete in organized swimming competitions. To encourage young swimmers to achieve excellence in swimming as well as academics. Safe Spor t Mountain Club Safe Sport Coordinator: Yaping Huang, z.lei@hotmail.com, (505)695-4042 T o deal with a Safe Sport concern , contact USA Swimming at (719)866-3542 To Contact US Center for Safe Sport to make a report, call (833)587-7233 or use Online Report Form To report anonymously, text anonymous tips to (888)270-7946 Mountain Club Safe Sport Minor Athlete Abuse Prevention Policy Safe Sport Best Practice Guidelines Written Acknowledgement of MAAPP Child Protection Policy Anti-bully Policy Locker Room Policy Photography Policy Electric Communication Policy Travel Policy Massage and Rubdown Policy One-on-One Interaction Policy Coach Code of Conduct Parent Code of Conduct Athlete Code of Conduct Emergency Plan Grievance Procedure Coaches’ and Officials’ Continuing Educations Parent Consent Forms Achievements Sixteen (16) New Mexico (NM) Swimming records. Twelve (12) individual high point first places in NM State Championships. Six (6) champions in NM State Xtreme Challenge Championships. Over 100 champions of individual swimming events in NM State Championships. Qualifiers for US Swimming Western Zone Select Camp. Qualifiers for US Swimming Section and Zone Championships. All-American Swimmers who are required for excellence in both swimming and academics. Qualifiers for NM State Swimming Championships. Mountain club had 24 qualified swimmers in the championships. We entered 21 of them with 110 individual events and 21 team relays. Our swimmers finished the 4th place as a team with 456 points. The results of all the teams in the championships are shown in the table at the right. Mountain Club swimmers in the Championships. Zdenek, Magnus, Javier, and Justin won the 1st place of Boys 12 & Under 400M Free Relay. Mothers of the swimmers are officials in the Championships. Justin Won the High Point 3rd Place. Mountain Club Won the 1st Place in NM Games 2024 The New Mexico Games 2024 (swimming) was held on June 16th (Sunday) at West Mesa Aquatic Center in Albuquerque. Mountain club won the first place, Duke City Barracuda finished in the second place, and Kraken Team earned the third place. Mountain Club had 27 swimmers with 81 individual events and 9 relays during this meet. The age groups are 8 & under,9-10, 11-12, 13-14, 15-18, and Masters age groups in 5 years increment. Here are our nine relay finishes: 1st & 3rd finish for Mixed 14 & under 200 Medley relays 2nd & 8th finish for Mixed 200 Medley relays 5th finish for Mixed 400 (8×50) Free relays 1st & 3rd finish for Mixed 14 & under 200 Free relays 2nd & 6th finish for Mixed 200 Free relays All our Mountain swimmers had achieved top 3 finishes in their age groups. CAC Locations Avila Bay Athletic Club & Spa The Hills Swim & Tennis Club La Madrona Athletic Club Ogden Athletic Club Ojai Valley Athletic Club Paso Robles Sports Club Pierpont Athletic Club Westlake Athletic Club Member Login 805-646-7213 [email protected] Schedules & Waivers Search --> Search --> Ojai Valley Athletic Club About Aquatics Fitness Pilates Join Services Massage Tennis Pickleball Contact Us Search Schedules & Waivers Member Login Sidebar Lessons Swim Team Request Information OJAI Heatwaves OJAI HEATWAVES is a year round swim team that provides youth competitive swimming for all ages and abilities with an emphasis on education, achievement, and community. Our goals are to offer our members the highest quality stroke instruction, create enthusiasm for competitive swimming, and offer the Ojai Valley community youth the opportunity to pursue swimming as a life-long sport. We emphasize personal goal setting, excellent technique, health, fun and friendship. If you are interested in joining the Ojai Heatwaves, please fill out the form below. Aquatic Director, Elin Cheverez will contact you with more information. We are members of Southern California Swimming (USA Swimming.) We offer non-competition, novice competition and high level competition options. We have four levels and offer practices Monday through Friday and offer different swim meet options for the different training groups. How to Join Ojai Heatwaves Parent Handbook (detailed program information) Practice Schedule click here » OJAI Heatwaves Team Store Facebook page Team website Contact Aquatic Director Elin [email protected] Elin Cheverez started swimming at age 4 and continued to swim competitively through high school in Walnut Creek, CA. She revisited the sport after becoming a member at OVAC and started swimming with the Ojai Masters. Swimming under Coach Rick Goeden , Elin enjoyed competing at Master's meets and earned a top 10 in the 200 LCM Breaststroke. In 2008 Elin started coaching under Ojai Masters coach Rick Geodon. In 2011 Elin became the Aquatic Director at OVAC and Rick Goeden passed on the youth swim team to Elin. Starting with only 8 swimmers Elin has grown the team to 60+ swimmers working with Head Coach Wenke Seider. Elin and Wenke enjoy working together to accomplish their mission of offering high quality technical training. Elin is an ASCA Level 2 Masters coach, and is so grateful to be continually learning from the incredible coaching staff of the Ojai Heatwaves and Ojai Masters. She loves to see kids progressing in a lifelong sport that offers valuable life skills, and feels lucky to be part of the Ojai Heat Waves! Head Coach Wenke Seider Growing up in Germany, Coach Wenke started swimming at seven years old. At the age of 12 she became the German Age Group National Champion in the 100 breaststroke. At 13 she joined the German Junior National Team and competed at the European Junior Championships, placing fifth in the 100 breaststroke. She joined the German National Team at age 15 and competed for Germany for the next few years in international competitions such as European Championships, World Cup, etc. During her high school years in Heidelberg (Germany), Wenke spent one year in Geneva,(Switzerland) training and competing for Geneve Natation. At 19 Wenke moved to France to study at the University of Paris and continued to swim for one of the major clubs in France (Dauphins de Creteil), competing at French Nationals and other meets. After receiving her College degree (DEUG) in Paris, she moved to Santa Barbara on a swimming scholarship for UCSB. There she became a two-time Big West Conference Champion, earned a BA in French Literature and later a Single Subject Teaching Credential, as well as a Master's degree in Education. From 1998 to 2008 Wenke worked at the Santa Barbara Swim Club coaching all levels (from novice to elite) and together with her husband Brandon helped run the team of over 400 athletes for two of those years. During her time coaching at SBSC she coached swimmers to the highest level of age group swimming (Junior Olympics, All Star Swim Festival, Pacific Coast All Stars and North American Challenge Cup). Many of her swimmers went on to swim in College. She has been coaching the youth swim team at the Ojai Valley Athletic Club since 2012. As a masters swimmer Wenke qualified for the 2000 US Olympic Trials in the 100 and 200 breaststroke and held several Masters World Records, as well as five Masters World Championship titles. ASCA Level 4. Coach Brandon Seider Coach Brandon grew up in Carpinteria, CA and has enjoyed a long-time love of the water, going back to 1980 when he first experienced the joy of surfing and the ocean. His career in Aquatics began in 1989 as a member of the opening-day staff at the newly built Carpinteria Community Swimming Pool, where he maintained employment until 2002. In 1995, Brandon was hired as a coach at the Santa Barbara Swim Club (SBSC), under nationally recognized coach, Ira Klein. From 1995 to 2002 Brandon coached the SBSC Senior Team, Masters Team and Novice Team, and is known for growing both the Novice and Masters Teams well beyond their capacity. In 2000 Brandon was awarded the Southern Pacific Masters Association (SPMA) Coach of the Year Award. This was the same year Coach Wenke received the SPMA Swimmer of the Year Award, due to her amazing accomplishments as a Masters Swimmer, breaking numerous World and National Masters Records, as well as qualifying for the US Olympic Trials in two events (not an easy achievement at any age, but especially at age 30!). In 2002, Brandon and Wenke became married, and Brandon accepted a position as the Sprint and Breaststroke Coach at UCSB, under legendary coach, Gregg Wilson. He experienced success while coaching the Sprint Group, including one of his athletes qualifying for and participating at Division I Women's NCAAs. In 2004, Brandon left UCSB to take on the position of Head Coach at the Santa Barbara Swim Club. Being given the opportunity to lead the team where his competitive swim coaching career started was one of his highest honors. Brandon thinks there is no greater joy than having the opportunity to help athletes of all ages become the best they can be, and is excited to return to swim coaching as a part time assistant to the Ojai Heat Waves Age Group and Senior Programs. Coach Meg McCormick Meg is a 4th generation Ojai resident raising her 4 daughters. She has always been passionate about sports from a young age including many junior lifeguard courses. As an adult she runs as well as swims and has completed 7 marathons in her free time. Meg is a self-taught swimmer at age 4 and even participated in swim class with her mom through the college when she was young. She later attended Ventura College after high school and swam during her time there. Meg started working at OVAC and continued to swim with her mom through the OVAC's master program with Coach Rick Geoden. Because of her prior years' experience working with children, she began working in the OVAC Kid's Club department. Coach Elin approached her with the opportunity as a swim instructor and she jumped at the chance. The fit was perfect due to the connection with the kids through Kid's Club and her passion of wanting to be a positive role model for kids which she wished she had more of growing up. Meg completed her WSI training and taught learn-to-swim and parent child classes for years at OVAC. She discovered her niche for teaching technique and started teaching pre- swim team groups for the Ojai Heatwaves. Meg also assisted with a couple seasons of swim and water polo through Nordhoff High School and coaches as well as serves as a board member for youth track team. Meg is a certified CPR instructor and teaches American Red Cross CPR for all of the OVAC employees. Currently she coaches the first 3 levels of the swim team; Novice I, Novice II, and Junior Levels. Teaching beginners the basics is an important task and Coach Meg has helped many children stay safe in the water and progress their swim careers. It has truly become a passion for her to help kids develop fundamentals and create a strong swimming foundation that not only creates lifelong skills but is also fun! Seeing the kids progress and move up to the higher levels and set goals makes her so proud. Want to Know More? text: Bruin Swim Club | Recreation Skip to Main Content UCLA Recreation Feedback Sustainability Give Now Search Website Search About About Us Contact Us News Employment Sponsorship Register Rec Membership Classes & Programs Fitness Passes Private Services MAC Passes MAC Private Member Services Rec Programs Recreation Programs Adaptive Rec Aquatics Competitive Sports Experiential Programs FitWell Instructional Classes Marina Aquatic Center Outdoor Adventures Youth Programs Facilities All Facilities Reservation and Rentals Open Rec Facility Policies Events Feedback Sustainability Give Now Search Website Search Home Rec Programs Aquatics Bruin Swim Club Bruin Swim Club Welcome to the Bruin Swim Club (BSC), a year around program with the 2 weeks closure over the winter break and observing all the government holidays. Bruin Swim Club is open to boys and girls ages 6 to 17 and combines a competitive spirit with training that is developmentally appropriate. Our high-quality coaching encourages the achievement of each individual and enforces athletic training, motivational support, and having fun. The minimum club requirement is ability to swim 50 yards freestyle. Contact Information If you have any further questions about Bruin Swim Club, please contact the Head Coach. For Membership questions, contact swimclubs@recreation.ucla.edu Coaches Julia Voitovitsch Head Coach jvoitovitsch@recreation.ucla.edu Ivan Podvalov Assistant Head Coach ipodvalov@recreation.ucla.edu Ben Forbes Sub/Assistant Head Coach Getting Started with Bruin Swim Club Rec Member Account New parent/guardians to Recreation will first need to create an account with UCLA Recreation then add their dependent(s) to their profile. Go to our site: https://secure.recreation.ucla.edu/ Click Sign In (the top right corner) then Sign Up at the bottom of the popup window Returning BSC members can access their Rec profile here . Tryouts & Group Requirements Tryouts are offered every Wednesday at Student Activity Center (SAC) at 6 PM. Registration required. Once your swimmer has completed the tryouts and has been approved to join the team, you will receive an email from the coach with instructions to register for monthly autopay BSC membership and all other Bruin Swim Club information and policies. Bruin Swim Club Tryout Registration Group Requirements Level 1 : Ability to swim 50 yards freestyle breathing to the side Level 2 : Basic knowledge of all 4 strokes and ability to swim 4 x 100 Freestyle on 2:20 Level 3 : 4 x 50 IM on 1: 15 interval and ability to perform an endurance test - 6x 100y freestyle on interval 1:50 min Level 4 : 8 x 50 IM on 1 min interval and ability to perform an endurance test of 8 x100 freestyle on interval 1:40min Swimmers will be tested/evaluated for an opportunity to advance to the next level based on their individual progress Membership Terms & Pricing AutoPay Membership Requirements & Pricing Bruin Swim Club Membership is for access to Bruin Swim Club practices only. No further facility access will be granted without a purchased Rec Membership. Membership Requirements: Proof of current USA Swimming Membership An updated CampDoc profile is required for each participant. NOTE: Swim Club Coaches manage the swim levels and schedules. Coaches will communicate all changes through the parent’s email on file in CampDoc. Monthly AutoPay Pricing for all BSC Levels: UCLA Student $175/session/monthly UCLA Faculty/Staff $225/session/monthly Alumni/Community $250/session/monthly AutoPay Membership Terms & Conditions AutoPay Membership Terms & Conditions AutoPay requires a 3-month minimum commitment. After three months, it is a month-to-month membership. Each month must be paid in full on the first business day of the month . A valid credit card must be saved to Rec profile upon membership enrollment. It is the member's responsibility to keep the payment card up-to-date for upcoming payments. APPLEPAY not accepted. No membership refunds, proration, discounts, or extensions for any facility and campus closures, including the annual winter closure. AutoPay Declined Payments Outstanding Payments: For all declined credit cards, Member Services will email the member on the first business day of the month. Member must update their payment card Recreation Profile and pay the outstanding invoice. REQUIRED : Email info@recreation.ucla.edu to confirm payment within 2 business days. If payment is not received by the 5th of the month, the BSC membership will be immediately terminated. AutoPay Cancellation Policy Cancellations due by the 15th - It is the member’s responsibility to submit the Cancellation Request Form prior to the 15th of the current month to avoid being charged for the following month. No exceptions. Email and phone requests are not valid cancellation requests. Form must be submitted to initiate cancellation. AutoPay memberships require a 3-month minimum commitment. Each month must be paid in full on the first business day of the month. Requests to cancel prior to 3-months will automatically result in a $30 cancellation fee to the saved card on profile. Membership holds are not available. Member must submit a cancellation request and can re-enroll into membership as needed. Refunds will not be provided for duplicate membership purchases. All Memberships are non-refundable and discounts and extensions are not offered for any facility or campus closures. If Recreation does not receive cancellation form, no cancellation will be processed. Refunds will be processed to saved card on file. For outdated/declined payment cards, Member services will contact customer via phone and email to collect new payment type. 90 days after submitting the Cancellation form, the refund is void. It is the responsibility of the member to ensure their personal contact information is up to date with Recreation. Contact information includes: current email address and phone number. Recreation is not responsible for missed communications due to out-of-date contact information. A refund up to 3 months of charges can only be considered for the following three exceptions. The first three months of membership are NOT eligible for any refunds. Member has separated from employment with the University, Member will be moving 50 miles or more from the facility (must provide documentation Member has a documented medical circumstance that will not allow them to use the facility. Bruin Swim Club Policies SWIMMER’S RESPONSIBILITIES The Bruin Swim Club has a ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY! Bullying, Sexual Harassment, and Misconduct of any kind WILL NOT be tolerated. The swimmer will receive a warning and be disciplined accordingly. If the issue persists the swimmer will be suspended from club activities. Never interfere with the progress of another swimmer either physically or verbally during practice or otherwise. Swimmers must be punctual for all practices and meets. Swimmers are to be dressed five minutes before the start of practice and on deck ready to practice per their coach’s instruction. Pay attention and follow instructions at all times. During practice sessions, swimmers are never to leave the pool area without the coach's permission. Follow instructions from the lifeguards and all posted safety rules, such as no running on the pool deck. Swimmers are expected to behave responsibly in the locker rooms. Use of the facilities is a privilege. Bruin Swim Club members are guests while on campus (both swimmers and parents). Every member of the club needs to respect this privilege. Damages to University property may result in financial liability for the swimmer's parents. Any damage may also result in suspension from Bruin Swim Club. No loitering in the bathrooms during practice. Any swimmer who is known to use alcohol, drugs, or tobacco is subject to suspension and/or expulsion from the team. At all club functions, whether practice, meets, or social gatherings, we expect each swimmer to behave in such a way that their actions reflect positively on the team. All members of the club, whether parents or swimmers are expected to protect and improve the integrity and reputation of the club. We do not prorate, no make up sessions or changing the days of the session. SUN SAFETY Please send your child to practice with waterproof sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher), with your child's name clearly marked on it. Helpful Suggestion: Try applying all-day waterproof sunscreen REMINDERS Punctuality is extremely important. Your child should arrive at practice on time, preferably 15 minutes prior to the scheduled workout time so that he/she will have sufficient time to change and check in for practice. Pick-up has to be no later than 15 min after the practice time. To ensure safety, well-organized, and effective coaching instructions, we have no parents on the deck policy. MEDICATIONS If your child requires medication during the practice and/or meets it must be noted on their emergency form. We are prohibited from dispensing over-the-counter medications or supplements. LOCKERS Day-use Lockers will be available at the Student Activities Center Pool. LOST & FOUND Lost and Found items are stored at the facility in which they were lost. After two weeks, unclaimed lost and found items are donated to charity. UCLA Recreation is not responsible for any items lost during practice or meets. We highly encourage you to not allow children to bring valuable items to practices or meets. All personal items should be clearly labeled with their first and last names in permanent ink. PARKING Parking is available for hourly use in Parking Lot 4. Parking can be purchased at the kiosk or by following the app directions posted. There isn’t an option for load in/load out or drop off/pick up. Parents are required to check in and pick up all swim club members. Children under 12 will not be allowed to leave without a parent present for pick up. MANDATED REPORTING UCLA Recreation employees are mandated by California State Law to report any suspected cases of child abuse or neglect directly to the appropriate authorities for investigation. While we have established internal procedures to facilitate reporting and apprising supervisors, we cannot by law require our employees to disclose his or her identity to anyone. SUN SAFETY Please send your child to practice with waterproof sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher), with your child's name clearly marked on it. Purchase UCLA Bruin Swim Club Gear Separately, you can visit the below online store where items will be mailed directly to you. UCLA Swim Cap Kick board - you can use any kick board you like ( maybe you already have one ) Junior pull buoy Floating fins Mesh storage bag Level 3 and 4 only: Youth Snorkel (Kids ages 12 under) Snorkel (Kids ages 12 and up) Swim Paddles (size S or M depends on your hand size) Philosophy To learn how to make swimming a lifestyle. By making swimming a lifestyle, you learn what it means to be committed and disciplined, how to live and enjoy the moment, and how to set long-term goals. We want our swimmers to have fun while they are working hard. The rewards will come through commitment, hard work, and enjoyment of this special sport. Goals: Swimmers receive excellent technique training in all swimming strokes. Swimmers gain strength and endurance in all swimming strokes. Swimmers learn the language of competitive swimming and interval training and how to pace themselves in meets. Swimmers are encouraged to become self-disciplined and self-motivated. Swimmers participate in a multi-age group club that promotes friendship and supporting one another. Mission and Vision Statement Megalodon Swimming is a program designed to help educate athletes in Competitive swimming (Butterfly, Backstroke, Breaststroke and Front Crawl) Give them a chance and opportunities to race at a high level while in a safe and supportive environment. To help each Athlete reach goals they will set with no to little team limitations. Megalodon Swimming is here to help athletes grow. Learning not just to swim, but to lead, teach and grow following all US Swimming guidelines and to take all the skill for personal growth. title: Home
text: Home Home Swim Team Our Team Parents Tools for Swimmers and Parents Coaches and Administration Officials Alumni Lessons Alchemy Swim Team Lessons Group Lessons Private Coaching Calendar Safe Sport OA Records Evaluations Contact Us Home Swim Team Our Team Parents Tools for Swimmers and Parents Coaches and Administration Officials Alumni Lessons Alchemy Swim Team Lessons Group Lessons Private Coaching Calendar Safe Sport OA Records Evaluations Contact Us LOGIN Transforming Potential Into Performance Training swimmers, athletes, and champions for life. ﻿ JOIN OA HERE oa swimming We are glad you found OA! OA is a year-round competitive swim team, offering high-quality professional coaching and technique instruction for all ages and abilities. Our goal is to give every member the chance to grow their skills and achieve success—whether just starting or competing at the national level. We strive to ensure our community thrives both in and out of the pool. Our Mission OA strives to create a positive environment where swimmers develop self-discipline, build good habits, and cultivate a love of sport that equips them for success in life. Our Vision OA aspires to be the best team experience in the world, developing athletes who become excellent people, ready to do excellent things. Our VALUES At OA, we value education, growth, discipline, love, gratitude, and excellence in everything we do. • Education – We teach life lessons through swimming. • Growth – We pursue constant improvement in and out of the pool. • Discipline – We believe in consistent habits and self-control. • Love – We foster a passion for swimming and respect for teammates. • Gratitude – We value every opportunity to learn, compete, and grow. • Excellence – We strive to be our best in all we do. title: Aquabear Swim Club | Home
text: Aquabear Swim Club | Home AQUABEAR SWIM TEAM Home The Facility Contact Us Swim Team Group Descriptions and Practice Times Meet Schedule Registration Information Coaching Staff Swim Lessons Training Equipment And Merch Lap Swim Summer Swim Team 2026 Pickleball Top 10 Team Times The Aquabear Swim Team (BEAR) is a year-round competitive swim team offering a multi leveled, and tailored swim program to meet the needs of each and every swimmer. BEAR also offers a recreational level program (with or without swim meets) during the summer, fall, and spring months, as well as year round swim lessons. The team operates out of both the Aquabear Swim Club (formerly Oracle Heights) , as well as the "Orange Grove Pool" (formerly Sunshine Swim School) on the northwest side of Tucson at two of longest standing and reliable facilities in Tucson. The Aquabear pool comprises a 5-lane 25 yard training and competition pool that is heated and maintained at a comfortable 80-82 degrees year round. It also offers a 30ft x30ft 12 ft "diving well" that is set up for an additional 5 lanes for beginner level swim team. The Orange Grove pool comprises an extremely comfortable 40ftx20ft teaching depth pool that is maintained at a teaching comfortable 82-84 degrees year round. We emphasize fundamental skills, physical conditioning, productive work habits, character growth, healthy competition, and most of all - enjoyment. BEAR swimmers compete in meets which are held locally, regionally and nationally. The Aquabear Swim Team focus is on producing a long term family of progressing swimmers-athletes receiving the benefits of lifelong health, social growth, and successful academic and athletic performance. Our goals for this team include the following (in no particular order): Top-level team pride and unity Excellent communication fun and positive environment High expectations of success for dedicated athletes Excellent technique and skills The ability for all the swimmers to compete in all the events offered in their age group Development of lifelong skills and attributes such as goal-setting, commitment, work ethic, and working together as a team Provide a safe, healthy, and positive environment for swimmers of all ages, free of bullying and any form of abuse. The "New Breastroke" ... by Gary Hall Sr. March 9, 2020 The New Breaststroke I love watching Adam Peaty and Lilly King do the swimming technique breaststroke . It is the new breaststroke. You might call it a high octane breaststroke, as it is a powerful swimming technique for the 50 and 100, primarily (Adam doesn’t even swim the 200 breast). This new breaststroke should be fast in both tempo and speed. Having a fast stroke rate in breaststroke does not necessarily equate to having speed. It is pretty easy to spin your wheels in breaststroke and waste a lot of energy without having much to show for that effort in terms of speed. Breaststroke is the most timing-sensitive of all four strokes. It requires a completely different set of tools to do well, which includes hip, ankle, and lumbar spinal flexibility. It is also a stroke where, in order to do well, neither the arms nor the legs ever get to rest. For all of these reasons, breaststroke is the most difficult stroke to teach and learn. Lilly and Adam have several things in common in their breaststroke technique. Both swimmers are very strong in the pull and the kick. Both swimmers use their upper bodies and heads extremely well to couple with the pull and the kick. Both swimmers have lightning fast legs. Having the right hip and ankle flexibility enables a breaststroker to push the instep of the feet backward with greater surface area, resulting in more propulsion. Having more lumbar flexibility enables a breaststroker to elevate the shoulders higher out of the water, while still keeping the legs pointing backwards. The higher the shoulders climb, the harder they fall. It is in the falling of the upper body and head where the timing becomes crucial for the kick. If the swimmer is to take advantage of all that energy of the upper body and head crashing down, there is precious little time from the end of the pulling propulsion; when the shoulders are fully elevated and legs pointing backwards, until the start of the subsequent kicking propulsion, when the upper body should be striking the water. Shortly after that, the kinetic energy of the upper body goes to zero. If the kick didn’t happen in time, you just missed the dance. That is where the lightning fast legs comes into play. Recently, using Pressure Meter technology at The Race Club, we measured the force on the pulling hands of world class Croatian breaststroker, Nikola Obrovac. By increasing his stroke rate by 4 strokes per minute (53 to 57) and by increasing the speed of elevation of his shoulders by 9% (207 degrees per second to 227 degrees per second), Niko increased the pressure (force) on his right hand by 9% and on his left hand by 3%. We will feature all of Niko’s results in an upcoming webisode. While Niko’s shoulder elevation is a coupling motion for his breaststroke pulling force, we presume that coupling will work for his kick, also, if the timing is right. To develop lightning fast legs for breaststroke requires great strength and training. Then, with those fast legs, to augment the power of the kick, the head must snap down hard and the body press forward vigorously. Yours in swimming, Gary Sr. https://theraceclub.com/aqua_note/the-new-breaststroke/ The Aquabears, the premier swim team in NW Tucson, practices at the Aquabear Swim Club under the direction of Justin Slade. Click here for more information USA Swimming year-round Competitive Swim Club - Adult MASTERS Swim - High School Swim Pre-Season Conditioning - Swim Conditioning for returning College Swimmers - Summer Swim Camp Summer Swim Camp registration and information available HERE Registration Registration for Aspire Aquatics Practice Schedule Meets and Events Registration 2026-2027 SC Meet Schedule 2026-2027 Short Course Meet Schedule About our Coaches Click to sign up for meets or team events Welcome Aspire Families! About Us Aspire Aquatics of Colorado offers 5 distinct programs to support the competitive swim team needs of our community. Please contact [email protected] to join: A year-round competitive swim team , led by head coach Karen Ammon, that serves ages 6-14 ("Age Group") and high school-level age 15+ ("Senior") swimmers. Summer Swim Camp for youth age 4-12 who are not participating on summer swim teams, but still would like to further their swim skills A high school swim pre-season conditioning program to support high school swim team athletes A MASTERS program for adults of various ages and abilities. Program is year-round and allows for rolling registration to join anytime A swim conditioning program for returning college students in the summer and over winter break to train with their like athletes and to meet distinct college conditioning needs We are located in southeast Denver Metro serving Centennial, Aurora, Parker, and other surrounding areas. We support swim growth and excellence within the community of Grandview High School and surrounding Cherry Creek School District and Douglas County School District high schools. Our Mission To provide a safe, nurturing, technique focused competitive swim environment that allows purposeful personal growth and development of leadership skills through intentional community engagement. Our Vision Inspiring Excellence, Creating Community, Building Leaders Our Strategic Commitments Aspire Aquatics seeks to combine the competitive nature and technical discipline of year-round swimming with the enjoyable team and community spirit enjoyed by other competitive swim environments (i.e summer clubs, high school programs, etc). These elements combined, lift our young athletes to aspire towards physical, mental and personal excellence in their sport, and more broadly in life. Emphasis will be on providing technical instruction in a supportive, respectful, and community-minded environment. Mental health in youth competitive environments is often overlooked and underserved; Aspire seeks to purposefully cultivate and prioritize a culture of support, safety, team and family comraderie while our athletes grow in their competitive spirit and performance. Coach Karen's expertise and strategies will be applied to all practice groups to create a top-down and unified coaching philosophy across the coaching staff. Coach Karen will have a presence on deck with all practice groups. In addition to swim performance excellence, Aspire Aquatics will promote: ​ For the Athlete: well-balanced development in performance, mental health, mind set, and nutrition education respectful and growth-minded deck experience strategic use of skill-sharpening practice equipment and race techniques reasonable coach to swimmers ratio growth in sportsmanship and team camaraderie a legacy of giving from older to younger athletes leadership and character development high school and collegiate swim readiness education For the Family: frequent parent communication involvement opportunities to lift swimmers to aspire shared community-building experiences that create lifetime bonds Sponsors Sponsors & Partners Contact Email: [email protected] Facebook Instagram ©2026 SportsEngine, LLC. Teens 13-15 years old may go through Teen Fitness Certification with parent consent which gives them access to specific equipment. Founded in 2000, Desert Storm Swimming (DSS) is a local year-round competitive swim team, from novice to the most skilled swimmers, ages 5 to 18. Workouts are held at the Las Vegas Municipal Pool (a 50-meter by 25-yard Olympic-sized indoor pool), centrally located at the corner of Bonanza and Las Vegas Blvd. Desert Storm Swimming is affiliated with USA Swimming, Inc. and is a member of the Desert Section, a division of Southern California Swimming. We compete in local, state, regional, and super-regional swim meets, including in the Las Vegas and Southern California areas and beyond. Welcome to east valley swim team! Welcome to east valley swim team! Welcome to east valley swim team! Speed comes easy when you put "Technique First." WE BUILD CHAMPIONS FROM SCRATCH. OUR A+ TECHNIQUE PROMOTES LONG-TERM SUCCESS! join the team Step 1 - Schedule an Evaluation Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Click here Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Click Here Step 3 - Registration Step 2 - Group Placement/Recommendation Step 3 - Registration check out our reviews Click here East Valley Swim Team Expands to Queen Creek CLASS IS LIMITED. SCHEDULE AN EVALUATION NOW! Great News! East Valley Swim Team Developmental 1-8B class is open for new students! EVST announces evaluations at the Gilbert location for their new class starting September 5, 2026. The East Valley Swim Team (EVST), which has become one of the most successful swimming programs in the Valley thanks to its emphasis on teaching superior stroke technique, is now accepting signups from swimmers between ages 5 and 14 for its developmental and competitive teams at the Gilbert and Queen Creek locations. Training sessions will be offered at the 2161 E Pecos Rd in Gilbert and Queen Creek pool (22343 E. Ryan Rd.) Registration for developmental 1-8 group is now in progress for the Gilbert location. The pool is heated for year-round use. Spots are limited and are on a first-come, first-served basis. Private lessons will also be offered. Interested parents should contact EVST at (480) 547-1623 or click East Valley Swim Team - Booking Appointments to schedule a free evaluation for their child. To qualify for Developmental level 1-8, a swimmer must be able to swim Freestyle with side breathing and backstroke for at least 12.5 yards and swim independently. Please contact EVST for the current schedule. Schedule subject to change, if needed. Home of accelerated swim instruction. Get results sooner! Tired of bringing your child to swim lessons or training for months or years with minimal or no progress? Save time and money - join East Valley Swim Team! Providing top-quality stroke instruction at a fast track pace, advancing swimmers more quickly than competitors. CALL (480) 547-1623 TO Schedule an evaluation Spots are limited. Call us at (480) 547-1623 now to reserve your spot. We are accepting new swimmers as space allows. Ask about our high school swimmers and beginner's class. The list is forming. Call (480) 547-1623 NOW to schedule an evaluation. A small team providing superior technique and quality instruction At East Valley Swim Team, we develop Champions from scratch! A great start means a great future! Subscribe Email Sign up What is East Valley Swim Team? At East Valley Swim Team, we have designed a quicker method to transform independent young swimmers 5 years of age and older from swimming backyard freestyle to competitive freestyle in as little time as possible. This method saves parents a lot of time and money. At East Valley Swim Team, we strive to provide superior stroke technique and instruction at an accelerated pace in all four competitive strokes so the swimmers can advance to the competitive level significantly sooner than competitors and with stroke technique that will provide them long term success. Our Story East Valley Swim Team was formed out of a need to provide displaced competitive swimmers a new home to fulfill their desires to achieve swimming excellence and reach their fullest potential. These elite swimmers’ former club changed its policy to allow “club members only,” which forced many of the team participants including Coach Maria to leave in search for a new pool. Through word of mouth, the resulting swim team steadily grew and a developmental group was formed to provide new, younger swimmers an opportunity to learn sound stroke techniques at a Fast Track pace, which opened up an accelerated option for these swimmers to advance to the competitive group. Mission Our coaching philosophy provides top-quality stroke instruction using a fast track system that advances young swimmers to the next skill level more quickly and encourages the development of each swimmer to his or her fullest potential. We encourage a small class size environment to promote individualized coaching at each skill level, resulting in a team of quality swimmers trained to achieve optimal performance. Due to our technique driven philosophy and accelerated program, many of our swimmers have achieved AZ State level status in just 2 to 2.5 years since graduating from our Level 1 program. That is unbelievable! Goal The goal of East Valley Swim Team is to share the Fast Track system of providing superior swim instruction with any young independent swimmer who want to dedicate themselves to reach their fullest potential in swimming. Testimonials When my boy transferred from another swim club to Coach Maria's club, he just had a little interest in swimming, the only reason he went to swimming practice was he wanted to have some play time with other kids in the swimming pool. But Coach Maria changed this. After a couple months with Coach Maria, I found my boy started to be eager to go to swimming practice, he told me he loved Coach Maria's lessons: hard but not boring, it was fun. After one year's practice with Coach, the improvements were so significant, my boy obtained the state qualifications on some events, he was so excited to be able to compete with top swimmers in this state. Coach Maria is very passionate about teaching these young swimmers, she has magic fingers to motivate kids loving swimming, focusing on details of techniques and trying hard on their extremes. She is very strict on the lessons, but is very nice and open when she is not on lessons, all kids love to talk with her and share what they do in their daily life. Actually, we all love her! Susan * * * My family has known Coach Maria for eight years now. She was the Age Group coach for my daughter at 7 years old. Aside from Coach Maria’s impressive years of coaching experience, we also speak highly of her true passion in helping young children become successful swimmers. Her ability to teach young children how to swim with great precision, form and technique is very admirable. It takes a great deal of patience and dedication to teach these swimmers to develop good swimming habits. We see all these great qualities in Coach Maria. She is very dedicated and works so hard to make these young swimmers successful in and out of the pool. Simonette Hicks * * * Maria is a very kind, compassionate and intuitive swim coach. She has helped me be comfortable in the water and have improved after just one session with her. Linda Chun * * * Before we joined Coach Maria, my son had been swimming for five years already. But he never got anywhere, not even to the “B list." The only reason I came to Coach Maria is that her team was nearest to my home. By then, I have already given up hope that swimming could lead my son anywhere. “Just for some exercise” is what I told Coach Maria when I joined the team. What I did not know is that I accidentally got Alex to a “fast track." In less than a year’s training with Coach Maria, he got to “B List” on almost all strokes, then a couple of “A-Lists." He even got to participate in this year’s State Championship. That is just unbelievable. Yu Meng * * * My son has been here since February and he loves it! The Coach is fantastic! She corrected his posture effectively! My son is eager to attend each class. Thank you Coach Maria! Swim Mom * * * Copyright © 2026 East Valley Swim Team, LLC - All Rights Reserved.
